...with assistance. They say, moreover, that the Sun and Moon both shine during the day in such a way that they do not hinder each other; yet when both are shining, the light is clearer. Then, more than the first philosophers imagined, God granted two materials: one for the red stone, the other for the white stone—just as He gave the Sun by day and the Moon by night. Each illuminates the world without the help of the other, yet they also illuminate the world when both shine, and neither hinders the other.

So, they took the red material alone and from it they composed the stone with the assistance of the white, as will be taught in the manifest work. Then they took the white material and from it they elicited the white stone without the help of the red material or of "combustible sulfur" <note>In alchemy, "combustible sulfur" often refers to impurities that cause metals to blacken or burn away; the "incombustible sulfur" mentioned on previous pages is the desired, stable essence.</note>. Thus, they discovered the composition of the white stone without the help of the red, though they were forced to give it the ferment of silver. Yet, this stone is not as subtle, nor does it achieve such a great "projection" <term>Projection</term> <note>The final stage of the Great Work, where a tiny amount of the Philosopher’s Stone is thrown onto a molten base metal to transform it into gold or silver.</note> as that white stone produced by the first philosophers, which was extracted from both of those materials. Nevertheless, the later work involves much less labor, a shorter time, less expense, and no danger. 

Thus you shall know, my son, and understand that the white stone alone can be prepared without the red, provided the ferment of silver is granted to it. The red stone, however, cannot be prepared without the assistance of the white, just as was taught before in the preface. Commit these secrets to memory. 

Know furthermore, my son, that there are many "sects" of philosophers <note>Groups or schools of thought following different alchemical traditions or recipes.</note>, and each of these had its own peculiar operations; yet all took one single material from which they composed the stone. There are short ways and long ways, but the more subtly you prepare the stone and the more you purify it, the greater its projection will be. One of the philosophers reduced it <note>This likely refers to the "multiplication" or "augmentation" of the stone's power.</note> to 10 parts, another to 20, and so on higher, according as they knew how to work well and purge their stone rightly—indeed even to 100,000, etc., and that from one and the same material.

In this way you will learn, my son, to extract the stone from the material with great subtlety; and when you have drawn it out, you shall purge it with great diligence and cleanse it with great subtlety. Then, with the highest diligence, you shall make it subtle and "more than subtle," and so you will be able to lead it to great powers. Now, reread the preface often so that you understand these things properly before you approach the work; do not run like a madman to the mastery of our art, but begin each thing in order with a stout heart...

### CHAPTER XVIII.

<margin>
What must be done next.

This stone must be dissolved in common distilled water.

The solution is to be poured into a large vessel, and 4 or 5 measures of common distilled water added. And the whole is to be gently boiled together over ashes for the space of half an hour.
</margin>

These things being so, take a large <term>receiver</term> <note>original: "receptaculum". A glass vessel designed to collect distillates or hold solutions.</note>. Having placed a glass funnel upon it, set the receiver in a <term>testa</term> <note>original: "testa". An earthenware pot or basin used to hold sand or ashes to distribute heat evenly.</note> with sifted ashes, over a furnace in which a strong fire can be kindled. Then take the glass in which your matter is contained and pour common distilled water over it; in the space of 2 or 3 hours, all will be resolved into a liquid water. Then pour it into that large receiver which is on the furnace in the pot with ashes. Once the glass bottle from which you emptied the matter is thoroughly washed, mix all the matter together in the large receiver. Then take 5 or 6 <term>quarts</term> <note>original: "quartarios". A standard liquid measure of the period.</note> of distilled water and pour it together into the large receiver over the dissolved matter, until 1 or 2 parts of the large receiver are filled. This done, set a fire under the furnace and increase it by degrees, until the matter with the water in the glass grows hot. Leave the glass open at the top so it does not burst, and let it boil moderately in this way for half an hour, and then cool on its own. When this is finished, leave the glass on the furnace for 3 natural days, and your matter will settle to the bottom; then a little...

...and afterward, the cooled water with its matter must be left in the vessel for 3 whole days. And all the matter will settle to the bottom.

### CHAPTER XIX.

<margin>Drying the stone by evaporation.</margin>
Next, empty your matter out of that large glass vessel and place it into 2 or 3 wide glass bowls. ### CHAPTER XX.

<margin>Dissolving the stone in distilled vinegar using a lukewarm bath.</margin>
Furthermore, have ready some sharp distilled wine vinegar, properly rectified so that no dregs remain. Put your matter into a large receiver and place it in the water bath, pouring a good quantity of that distilled vinegar over the matter. Then cover your glass with a piece of polished glass. Build a fire under the bath, providing a heat equal to that of human blood or urine <note>This refers to a gentle heat of approximately 37–40°C (98–104°F).</note>. Do not let the water of the bath boil any further; keep it at this temperature day and night, and your matter will eventually dissolve. You will know this has happened when the

<margin>The sign of dissolution is a blue color in the vinegar.</margin>
vinegar takes on a blue color tending toward green <note>original: "colore ceruleo tendente ad viridem." In alchemical theory, this appearance of color (the "Iridis" or peacock's tail) indicates the internal essence of the metal is being released.</note>. This is the first color that reveals itself in the work. Note this sign, for it is a good sign; it shows that your matter is properly <term>putrefied</term> and "dead" within its white water, and that

<margin>The dissolved part is to be separated from the undissolved by pouring off.</margin>
it is so entirely dead that it can never again be reduced back to its original body. This is a good omen. For as soon as any colors appear in the work, we are certain that our matter has been <term>mortified</term> <note>original: "mortificatam." The process of "killing" the metal—stripping its outward form—so its inner soul can be transformed.</note>, that its interior is stretching outward, and that the putrefaction was successful. When this is done, have a large glass vessel ready, into

<margin>The dissolved part must be kept in a lukewarm bath.</margin>
which you should gently pour off the colored vinegar by tilting. Then immediately seal it well and place it in a lukewarm bath. Pour fresh vinegar over the remaining matter again, doing as you did before, and repeat this process...

# CHAPTER XXI.

<margin>The removal of vinegar through distillation until it reaches full dryness.</margin>

At this stage, <term>Luna</term> <note>original: "Luna." Literally "The Moon," the alchemical name for silver or the "White" stage of the Great Work.</note> is ready to be distilled through an <term>alembic</term> <note>A lid or apparatus used for distillation, often shaped like a helmet with a beak.</note> into an oil, and even to be reduced into crystalline, fusible stones. Then dry your matter in a basin with sand placed over a water bath; in this way you will lose no spirits. When the matter is dry and subtle, take a little of it, put it into a small vial, and pour over it common distilled water that has been purified so that nothing remains—the water ought to be rectified in this way. Over that which remained at the bottom of the glass, pour distilled vinegar, and let it sit in the vinegar again; when it has dissolved, distill the vinegar again, and pour common water over it once more. Resolve what is willing to be resolved, and if it all refuses to resolve, act in all ways as previously stated, until everything is dissolved in common water, and into a liquid water, so that no dregs remain in the bottom...

<margin>
The reduction of the stone into oil through dissolution and congealing in vinegar.

The <term>fixation</term> <note>The process of making a volatile substance stable under heat.</note> of the stone.

But because we do not know this matter <note>referring to the "natural" stone found in nature</note>, nor can we acquire it, another must be taken and prepared, as was said before, and rendered better and more subtle than even that stone which God gave us for free. Silver.</note>. # M. JOHANN ISAAC.

Take a firm, wide glass jar <note>original: "ollam"</note> which has a broad bottom, and place your matter into it, as I shall easily explain to you in person. Upon the jar, place a large <term>alembic</term> <note>The top part of a still, used for cooling and directing vapors.</note> with a wide beak <note>original: "rostro"</note>, and a receiver vessel attached to it with <term>lute</term> <note>A specialized sealant paste made of clay and other materials to make the joints airtight.</note>.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of an alchemical apparatus. It shows a rounded glass alembic with a long, straight beak or rostrum extending downwards to the right. This alembic sits atop a flared, conical base which represents the lower glass vessel (olla) or the furnace base.</image-desc>

The lower glass jar should be quite low, flat, and very wide at the bottom, as this figure demonstrates to you. Put your prepared materials into this, and once the alembic is placed on top, seal it properly with lute. Place it in the <term>sublimation</term> <note>The process of heating a substance so it rises as vapor and solidifies again at the top of the vessel.</note> furnace with a pan of ashes <note>original: "testa cinerum"; used to distribute heat evenly and prevent the glass from cracking.</note>. Glue the receiver to the beak with lute, and once the lute is dry, you are ready for sublimating. Concerning this matter, a certain Philosopher says: "The Earth is the lowest world, and the water, which ascends upward, has a soul within itself." Nor are there more than two known things, two in the open and two in secret, as is also evident in the elements: earth and water are known, for they can be seen and touched; but fire and air are hidden. So it is also in our <term>Stone</term> <note>The Philosopher's Stone.</note>: three things are seen clearly, and two are perceived obscurely. How then can they be seen? Just as it appears to the sight that <term>whiteness</term> <note>original: "albedinem"</note> lies hidden beneath <term>blackness</term> <note>original: "nigredine"</note>, and afterward <term>redness</term> <note>original: "rubedinem"</note> which was hidden beneath the whiteness. Those two were first in the intellect, but now they are visible to the eye.

<margin>First operation.</margin>
My son, how are the hidden sayings of the Philosophers to be understood? They said, in the first reduction—that is the one they called "solution," and it is the foundation of the art. Regarding this, <term>Rhazes</term> <note>original: "Rafis"; a 9th-century Persian physician and alchemist.</note> says: "Unless you dissolve the body, you labor in vain." For bodies must be reduced to such waters as those from which they first took their origin, that is, into common water. However, the common people do not grasp this solution. And this is its first reduction into its own essence, etc.

<margin>2. Operation.</margin>
Another Philosopher says: "Unless earth is produced from the thickness of the water, you are wasting your effort in our art," etc.

<margin>3. Operation.</margin>
The third work is purification or cleansing <note>original: "mundificatio"</note>. <term>Morienus</term> <note>A legendary 7th-century alchemist known for his dialogues with King Khalid.</note> says: "When this earth putrefies with earth, and is thinned, then—"

*Geber* <note>An influential 8th-century Arabic alchemist, often cited as an authority on chemical processes.</note> says: take away its humidity, and lead it immediately to sublimation, and draw from it the spirit which you find in it, which is called the **bird of Hermes**. <note>A symbolic name for the volatile spirit or vapor that rises during heating.</note> And of this *Morienus* <note>A legendary 7th-century hermit and alchemist.</note> says: there will remain to you calcined earth and sand. ### CHAPTER XXIII.

<margin>
Return to the work.
Sublimation of the Stone through its degrees of fire, until whatever is volatile is sublimated from the dregs.
The dregs are to be dissolved in vinegar, so that what is not sublimated may be drawn out from the dregs of sublimation, which is the earth of the Stone.
The sublimated matter is its spirit or the element of water.
Both must be kept separate until they are to be joined again.
</margin>
Now, my son, let us return to our work: you shall apply fire to the furnace, at first a little and gradually more through degrees, until you see your matter begin to <term>sublimate</term> <note>To transform from a solid to a vapor and then back to a solid on a cooler surface.</note>. Then maintain the fire at that heat as long as it ascends; but rather increase the fire a little than let it cool. And as long as you see it ascending, leave it thus with the moderate fire mentioned; and when the ascent itself begins to decrease, increase the fire as you see is necessary. You will be able to see this through the glass <term>alembic</term> <note>The lid or "head" of the distilling apparatus.</note>. Leave it thus night and day, always increasing the fire as you see it is necessary. 

When you see it no longer sublimates, increase your fire gradually until your glass jar <note>original: "olla"</note> glows red-hot <note>original: "candeat"</note> from below. Maintain it in that glowing state for two hours, or until you see it no longer ascends. Then allow it to cool of its own accord, and with the alembic removed, empty the vessel and store the contents in a glass box. Take the dregs <note>original: "fæces"</note> out of the glass jar and place them in a large glass vessel, and pour over them strong distilled vinegar made from wine. Place this in a warm <term>balneo</term> <note>A "bain-marie" or water bath, providing gentle, indirect heat.</note> and leave it to dissolve for eight days. Then pour the vinegar into a glass vessel and set it to <term>coagulate</term> <note>To thicken or solidify by evaporating the liquid.</note> upon the bath in a basin with sand until it is dry.

You should also know, my son, that when you place the materials to be sublimated, they must be mixed with the kind of material that is of such a nature that it preserves your prepared matter from melting. For you have made your matter so subtle that it would melt like butter even at a low fire. Therefore, the material through which you will sublimate the matter of the Stone must be prepared in such a way that it does not pollute your matter in the least, and so that nothing of this material ascends, and so that it cannot be destroyed by any fire, however great [a fire you apply] to it...

submitting it to the fire: it must furthermore be so prepared that glass cannot be made from the material, nor salt extracted from it: it must also be prepared so that it cannot be dissolved by anything, and so that it sheds no dregs from itself. Also, prepare it so that it is intangible <note>original: "intangibilis"; likely meaning a state of such purity or fineness that it does not react with common physical substances</note>: and if, my son, you do not have such a material, you will not be able to sublimate your prepared matter. <margin>The earth of the stone is to be weighed, as well as its spirit or the sublimate from the earth.</margin>
Therefore, my son, when you have drawn the spirit out of the material, place everything you find in the jar to be dissolved, and dissolve the body from the material from which you sublimated the spirit. Afterwards, also remove all the dregs and weigh them as well; thus you will be able to know clearly how the matter stands, and what you are lacking, whether everything has been drawn out or not. Attend to this diligently, and do not be reluctant to write anything down; thus what you have done can always be clear to you, and if you have any doubt about the work, you can imagine from a failed outcome why it happened, and amend it wherever you can.

### CHAPTER XXIV.

Know furthermore, my son, that you can make the material from which you extract your spirit so subtle, and so spiritual—first in its white water, in which it is placed in <term>putrefaction</term> <note>The stage of the alchemical process where the matter is allowed to rot or break down, often turning black, to prepare it for transformation</note>, and then in dissolution in vinegar—that in sublimation the whole of it ascends, so that it leaves nothing behind except the dregs. Therefore, you shall dissolve the matter in vinegar after the sublimation is performed, and you shall dissolve the earth or dregs from the material through which you sublimated; thus you will easily see whether all the matter of the stone has sublimated upward or not. For in the material through which you sublimated, nothing else is dissolved except what remained in it from the matter of the stone which was sublimated from it: and see that it is done as was said before.

### CHAPTER XXV.

<margin>The sublimation of the stone by itself without added dregs, and that by a slower fire.</margin>
You shall also keep, my son, in a glass vessel that which you dissolved from the material through which you sublimated: then take that which you sublimated upward, and place it again to be sublimated, first with a tiny fire, increasing it by degrees, until everything that can be sublimated has been carried upward.

<margin>The dregs left behind in this sublimation are to be added to the earth of the stone mentioned above.</margin>
Furthermore, my son, you shall sublimate the substance alone so that nothing else is present or mixed in; but add the remaining dregs to that which I commanded you to keep—that which you drew out with vinegar—and repeat the sublimation as many times until everything rises, so that nothing remains: then it is enough: then you have that Mercury from which the Philosophers extract their stone, then you have the incombustible sulfur, then you have the stone for the white work <note>original: "lapidem ad album"; refers to the stage of the Great Work producing silver or a white tincture</note>: and the Sages called this spirit water, and the white thing, and arsenic, and they bestowed many names upon it, such as sulfur [or] virgin’s milk.

<margin>This sublimation must be repeated until the stone leaves no dregs behind.</margin>
And that pure sublimate will take the place of the Mercury of the Philosophers: and it is also the incombustible sulfur.

### CHAPTER XXVI.

<margin>All the earth from the aforementioned sublimations must be reverberated until it reaches the whiteness of snow.</margin>
Likewise, you shall now take, F. M. <note>likely an abbreviation for "Fili Mi" (My Son)</note>, all that earth and the dregs which you kept from the first sublimation, drawn out with vinegar, together with all other dregs which you left in the other sublimations; you shall take them all together and set them to be reverberated <note>original: "reuerberandas"; a process of heating in a furnace where the flames are reflected or "reverberated" onto the material to reach high temperatures</note> until they become as white as snow; then let them cool: take them from the furnace, and place them back in glass, set it in a bath <note>original: "balneo"; a water bath or "Bain-Marie" for gentle, indirect heating</note>, and pour over it sharp distilled vinegar, properly rectified.

<margin>The solution of the reverberated earth in a bath by means of vinegar.</margin>
Kindle the bath moderately, and your vinegar will become slightly green: then let it cool, and pour it out by tilting <note>original: "inclinatione"; decanting or pouring off the liquid while leaving the sediment at the bottom</note> into another glass, seal it and set it aside, and again pour in other vinegar, and place it in the bath once more, as before; and when the vinegar has again lost its color, pour it out again by tilting, and add it to the previous vinegar, and repeat this same thing until your vinegar is no longer stained by the color of the substances.

<margin>The dissolved earth, after evaporation, is to be reverberated again for a space of 24 hours and dissolved once more, as above.</margin>
Then dry the dregs and again set them to be calcined <note>burned to a powder to remove impurities</note> for 24 hours; then let them cool, extract them from the furnace, place them again in glass, set them back in the bath, pour vinegar over them once more, and set them to be dissolved as before, doing in all ways as you did before. It will be necessary, however, to pour on and pour off, and to calcine the dregs, until your vinegar is no longer [stained] by the color...

M. ISAAC HOLLANDUS.

<margin>
This burning (reverberation) and dissolution must be repeated until the earth leaves no dregs behind in the solution. After the final dissolution and evaporation, a most beautiful and shining earth will remain.
</margin>

...is tinted. Therefore, pour a small amount into a glass crucible, then place it upon hot ashes and see if it evaporates completely. If so, you have entirely removed the earth from the dregs. Once this is done, thicken (coagulate) your vinegar, and an excellent white powder will remain for you. Place this powder again to be burned (calcined) in a reverberatory furnace <note>A furnace that reflects heat onto the material rather than applying direct flame</note> for 24 hours with a moderate heat, so that it only glows white-hot; do not use an intense heat, lest it melt (liquefy). Then allow it to cool and take it out of the furnace. Place it to be dissolved in distilled (rectified) vinegar in exactly the same way as described above. You shall dissolve it and again freeze it into a solid (congeal), and then burn it to powder (calcine) so many times until you find no more dregs remaining in the bottom of your glass. When everything is finally dissolved together so that no dregs remain, thicken it once more, and there will remain for you a distinguished, shining, clear earth—the very body of your stone. And this is what Morienus <note>A legendary 7th-century alchemist, said to be the teacher of the Umayyad prince Khalid ibn Yazid</note> means when he says:
> Do not despise the ashes in their lower state; and again: extract the ashes from the ashes, and in them you shall find a most beautiful diamond.

### CHAPTER XXVII.

<margin>
To one part of the earth, join three parts of the aforementioned sublimated spirit.
</margin>

Now know, my son, a great secret: you must take three parts of water—as the Philosophers have said, for they call the Spirit "water"—and one part of your prepared earth or "body." That is to say, you shall take and weigh all your earth or body to determine its weight, then take three times as much of your spirit as the weight of your earth.

### CHAPTER XXVIII.

Furthermore, you will not retain much earth or body from the 4 pounds <note>original: "℔.", the symbol for a libra or pound</note> of material which you originally put in, but however little it may be, you shall have enough to finish your work. For the earth possesses such great power (virtue) that even the tiniest amount is sufficient.

### CHAPTER XXIX.

<margin>
The lifting (sublimation) of the spirit with the earth through its proper stages of fire.
</margin>

And when, my son, you have ground the earth or body in that manner, you shall mix them thoroughly together—that is, the earth with the spirit—while dry upon a stone. Alternatively, you may dissolve and mix those two materials together and then dry them (congeal) until they can be turned into powder. Truly, that is not necessary; simply mix them dry upon a glass table. Once they are thoroughly mixed, place them together to be lifted by heat (sublimated). Apply first a tiny fire, and then gradually a larger one by degrees, and lift whatever is willing to be sublimated; and when it is sublimated further...

### CHAPTER XXX.

Likewise, a large quantity of material must be possessed and prepared from the beginning for this reason: because this work must be performed together with the spirit, and at the very least, all the earth must be drawn up together with the spirit, and afterwards "waxed" <note>original: "incerari," a process of adding liquid to a dry powder until it has the consistency of soft wax</note> with the spirit often and many times before the stone will become liquid and subtle, for which a large supply of spirit is necessary, etc.

### CHAPTER XXXI.

<margin>
Fermentation of the stone joined with its earth.
</margin>
Now indeed it is time that the soul or spirit be placed into the body that has been prepared together with its spirit, and that is the ferment. *Arnold of Villanova* <note>A famous 13th-century physician and alchemist</note> says on this matter:
> When the spirit is prepared together with the body, put the soul into it, so that it may rise again from death into one body, so that it may live forever; then all its enemies shall enter into peace with it.

Silver is to be taken for the ferment.
For calcining the Silver.
Calcination of Silver with common salt.

Set it to be calcined <note>Reduced to a powder through high heat</note> moderately so that it does not melt, for 3 continuous days. Then take it out and wash away the salt with hot water; and if any uncalcined part remains, put it back in as before. Then dry your powder over a small fire; then take twice as much prepared salt and mix it with your powder, and again set it to be calcined in a crucible...

### CHAPTER XXXIII.

<margin>Equal parts are to be taken of the ferment and the stone which is united with its earth, to be ground together on a glass tablet. The ferment and the stone joined together are to be placed in a vessel sealed with the seal of Hermes <note>An airtight seal created by melting the glass neck of the vessel</note>. The placement of the stone in the fixation furnace <term>fixatoria: a furnace designed to provide steady, even heat to make a substance stable under fire</term>.</margin>

<image-desc>An alchemical glass vessel with a spherical bottom and a long, slender neck containing two bulbous joints and ending in a small loop.</image-desc>

Now truly, my son, take the spirit with the earth or body which you sublimated together, and weigh them, or put them on a scale <note>original: "bilanci"</note>, and place the prepared Moon [Silver] on the other side of the scale. Equalize the weight of both, for both must be of the same weight—namely the ferment and the spirit together with the earth or body. Then mix them together on a glass table, and cast them into a glass of this kind, and compress it near the end at the roundness of the belly where it is narrowest: then place it in a pot with sifted ashes, to a measure of half a foot under the ashes. Place the pot in such a furnace that heats equally from below and above, which is called a fixation furnace, and push the neck out through the furnace so that the glass can be rotated often, both by day and by night.

### CHAPTER XXXV.

<margin>Observation of the colors.</margin>
And when, my son, you wish to see the colors manifesting themselves in the work, remove the cover of the furnace, and then replace it. And as often as the stone changes color, you shall increase the fire a little, until everything remains below, and everything is fixed at once. Truly, you shall write down all changes and colors, and you shall note the time passing between each one, and the time of fixation. And whatever you do, do not build a large fire until everything is fixed and brought to a white color.

<margin>Exact management of the fire.</margin>
<margin>The span of time in which the stone is to be fixed, namely 40 days, or at most 60.</margin>
And if you wish to work in a "blind furnace" <term>fornax caeca: an enclosed furnace designed to provide steady, indirect heat without exposing the vessel to an open flame</term>, as was said before, add fire to it day and night, such that you can keep your hand between the vessel and the walls of the furnace without having to pull it away. Within the space of one day and night, the glass must be inverted even twenty times: and this must be managed until everything is fixed together. Or you may put your matter into a glass egg <note>original: "ouo vitreo"; a round-bottomed, egg-shaped flask</note> and hang it in the secret furnace for 40 days at the aforementioned heat. Once these are finished, break it and see if your matter is fixed; if not, place it again in the secret furnace for 20 days, then it will be properly fixed. Thus you can fix your stone in 3 ways. But I advise you to place it in the furnace with a lid, so you can see the changes of the stone and its colors, and its entire management, because it is the first time you are working, so that you may see and write everything down.

<meta>This page continues the technical instructions for the alchemical "Great Work," specifically addressing the stage after the matter has been "fixed." # THE MINERAL WORKS

...purified to whiteness and prepared; and they joined the work together and fixed it. All of them saw the tints <note>original: "tincturas," referring to the color changes indicating progress</note> which the stone is meant to show, and they wisely fixed them. Having done this, they thought they had satisfied the requirements according to the doctrine of the Philosophers. And then they wished to perform the projection <term>projection: the final stage of alchemy where the finished "Stone" is cast upon base metal to transmute it into gold or silver</term>, but in vain. For the stone made no projection; and they abandoned the work, repeatedly saying that the art was impossible. And truly, this was so for them, for they did not understand nature. They did not recognize that the ferment <term>ferment: a substance, often purified gold or silver, added to the alchemical "stone" to give it a specific "direction" or quality</term> was not yet volatile <term>volatile: a substance that easily vaporizes or rises when heated; in alchemy, this represents the "spiritual" or "active" state</term>, nor had it been. They do not understand the words of the ancients when they say: "Our stone consists of body, soul, and spirit, and these are and will be one essence, and something inseparable."

<margin>
The fixed stone must now be made volatile again so that it becomes of the same quality as the ferment.
</margin>
Therefore, the ferment must also be volatile and fleeting, just as the body and spirit were. And they abandon the work when it is fixed; they are unable to perceive that the fixed matter or stone must be made fleeting again for the sake of the ferment that will be placed in it. Although the spirit is fixed with the body, they are not yet gathered with the ferment. For the ferment was not yet volatile, and until then they are not truly gathered. Believe no writings or words otherwise: for whoever tells you anything else will deceive you. The ferment must perish <note>that is, lose its original form or "die" to be reborn</note> with the spirit and the body, or the earth; otherwise, you play at your labor in vain. And in ascending, it becomes subtle and of great virtue, and is united to its body.

<margin>
The Sages called the ferment the "soul."
</margin>
For this reason, the Sages called the ferment the "soul" when they say: "the spirit draws the soul into the higher regions, and it descends again into the lower." Nature must be followed. Will there be a glorified body—enduring until the last day and for eternity—unless it is entirely subtle, and in such a way that it never dies? And will the soul remain as coarse in its first state as it was in the body on the earth? It cannot be; it must be as volatile and spiritual as the spirit. If we seek something other than what Almighty God made in His oridnance, or something other than what nature teaches us, we are deceived. But the ancients followed nature as much as they could; therefore they reached the good end of the work, and their prayers were granted.

### CHAPTER XXXVI.

<margin>
Nature must be imitated so that the stone becomes volatile.
</margin>
Now, my son, follow nature also as much as you can, so that you may likewise reach the desired end. Thus it will happen that you regret none of your labor, as you make the fixed stone volatile once more:

# MASTER JOHANNES ISAAC

<margin>Let one part of the fixed stone be sublimated with the 3 spirits mentioned above until the whole thing becomes volatile, always adding 3 parts of the volatile spirit to the remaining fixed part after sublimation; thus, the ferment will also become volatile.</margin>

<margin>The body, spirit, and soul must sublimate upward together so they become of one nature. Once sublimated and united, they become 1,000 times more refined than before.</margin>

Likewise, when you wish to make your earth, body, ferment, or any other fixed part of the Stone volatile, take 3 parts of the volatile substance and 1 part of the fixed. Mix them together and place them over a moderate fire for sublimation <term>sublimation: the process of heating a solid until it turns into a vapor and then solidifies again, used here to purify and "spiritualize" the matter</term>, just as I taught you before when you carried the earth upward with the spirit. When the spirits or volatile parts outnumber the fixed parts, they pull the fixed parts upward with them. Since the fixed parts are pure and clean, and the volatile parts are also pure and clean, and because they share one nature, they desire to remain together. Thus, the volatile substance draws the fixed one to itself more easily and converts it into its own nature. Once you have sublimated it, you can weigh what remains and did not ascend. Then, take three times as much spirit as there is fixed matter remaining, and set it to sublimate again as before. Repeat this until everything has been sublimated together. Do this with your fixed matter or stone, and draw its ferment <term>ferment: a substance added to the alchemical work to provide a specific "seed" or quality, often gold or silver</term> up with it so they become of one nature. For if the ferment had not been entirely sublimated along with the spirit and body, they would not be of one nature, even if they were fixed together. Once they have been completely sublimated together, they can never be separated. In the process of ascending, they are made a thousand times more refined <note>original: "subtiliora," meaning more purified, less dense, or more "spiritual"</note> than they were before.

### CHAPTER XXXVII.

And when, my son, you have sublimated one with the other upward, then place all those materials again into the fixing-glass to be fixed <term>fixed: a state where a substance no longer vaporizes when heated, having become stable and permanent</term>, as was taught before, and then the rectification <term>rectification: the process of refining a substance to its highest purity through repeated processing</term> will occur. Then all the colors that can be imagined in the nature of things will show themselves, followed by the **Peacock’s Tail** <note>a famous alchemical stage where the matter in the flask displays a shimmering, iridescent array of colors like a peacock's feathers, signaling the transition to the final stage</note>. Then the colors will begin to fade gradually, and sometimes they will finally reach a white color; then you may rejoice, for your Stone is now fixed.

### CHAPTER XXXVIII.

<margin>Another fixation of the aforementioned stone, where various colors will appear. When the colors show themselves—</margin>

Now know, my son, that many others have undertaken this work who were even sharper than the first ones. They brought their stone to the point described before and rejoiced, thinking they truly possessed the Stone. They cast it upon Mercury and upon Jupiter <note>the alchemical code name for the metal Tin</note>, but they achieved nothing. For their stone would neither dissolve nor enter the metal. They came to despise the art, saying it was impossible. But if they had understood the words of the Ancients where they say: "Moisten the lowest world with dew" <note>original: "Humecta mundum infimum rore," an allegorical instruction to add a "spiritual" liquid to the dry "earthy" matter</note>, then the stone would be fixed. Obstacles to inceration <term>inceration: the process of softening a dry substance by gradually adding liquid until it has the consistency of wax</term> and their remedy.

[...and let it be nourished] until it bears white, yellow, and red flowers. They say likewise: Nourish the king with his own milk until he has grown. Item: Let the earth be drenched with the clear and clean water of Paradise <note>The "water of Paradise" is an alchemical metaphor for the highly purified mercurial solvent or "spirit" used to wash the matter.</note>, and that water will ascend again to heaven, and again descend and dew the earth, so that it will be fertile and produce little flowers of various colors, by whose scent the King of Glory <note>The "King of Glory" refers to the perfected Alchemical Stone in its final state.</note> will be comforted, so that he will rise again from death and live again together with his wife, and the king will remain forever.

<margin>
**The waxing (inceration) of the fixed stone.** Three parts of the fixed stone are to be taken and one part of its volatile spirit, and they are to be fixed together. After this, the same work is to be repeated conversely, always with three parts fixed and one part volatile; and this is done so many times until the stone flows upon a glowing plate of Venus <note>original: "lamina Veneris"; in alchemy, Venus is the symbol for copper. A "glowing plate of Venus" is a heated copper plate used to test the Stone's quality.</note> and tints it.
</margin>

In this way, my son, when your stone is fixed, you shall take it from the fire and weigh it to see how heavy it is. Then you will take for every three parts of your stone one part of the spirit, and put them mixed together in the fixing-glass; thus, that one part of spirit will be fixed together with the stone, and this will happen easily. You remember those things I taught you before: When you wish to make something fixed become volatile, you take three parts of your spirit for one fixed part, and thus the volatile parts pull the fixed parts upward. Conversely, to make something volatile become fixed, three fixed parts will retain one volatile part with them and fix it. Since they will then be of one complexion and nature, and led to extreme purity and subtlety, they immediately embrace each other at the bottom of the vessel.

When you have now fixed this part, you will add another part to it, always taking three fixed parts for every one volatile part. You will repeat that so long and so many times until your stone flows over a glowing plate of Venus and penetrates it, just as oil penetrates dry leather. Then you may exult, for you have truly prepared the Stone of the Philosophers.

### CHAPTER XXXIX.

<margin>
From this entire process, one can consider the quantity of matter to be prepared for the perfecting of the stone.
</margin>

Now, my son, you yourself can notice how much matter must be put in at the beginning to complete the entire universal work. See how much spirit is required: for first a large part must be fixed with the earth; then the spirits that are fixed to the earth must be drawn upward together with the spirit, always taking three parts of spirit for every one fixed part. Then the ferment is added to the universal matter once the fixed parts have been fixed together. These also must all be made subtle again, and always three parts of spirit for one fixed part are to be taken, until all your fixed matter has been made volatile, and so on. But when everything has finally become volatile, then it is all fixed once more; and when all is fixed, it must be waxed <note>original: "incerandum"; the process of "inceration" or "waxing" involves adding liquid to the dry powder until it reaches a consistency like wax or butter, allowing it to melt without vaporizing.</note> with the spirit many times over, until your stone flows like wax or butter. All these works must be performed by means of the spirit.

It emphasizes the specific 3:1 ratios of fixed to volatile matter required to ensure the "King" (the Stone) can penetrate metal like oil into leather.</summary>

<header>MASTER JOHN ISAAC [HOLLANDUS].</header>

And although I spoke of 4 lbs of matter, perhaps 7 or 8 lbs would be needed before the work might be brought to its end; for if we were in the middle of the work and the spirits were to fail, then the work would have to be interrupted until fresh matter was set and prepared as before, and that would be a long process. Therefore, take as much matter at the beginning as may be sufficient for you.

## CHAPTER XL.

<margin>The stone is not to be made too fusible so that it can be projected upon Jupiter.</margin>
You shall also know, my son, that your matter must not be made too fusible. You shall make your projection <note>The "projection" is the final stage of alchemy where a small amount of the Stone is cast upon molten base metal to transmute it.</note> upon Jupiter <note>original: "Iovem"; in alchemical notation, Jupiter represents the metal Tin.</note>; for this is the body closest to the Moon <note>The Moon represents Silver.</note>, and the purest body of all the imperfect ones. It is crude and poorly cooked in the mine; therefore it shrieks when it is bitten into <note>original: "stridet, cum in eo mordetur"; this refers to the "tin cry," a characteristic crackling sound made when bending or biting pure tin, which alchemists interpreted as a sign of its "crude" nature.</note>, and it is full of whiteness. For this reason, make your projection onto Jupiter, for in it this medicine has nothing else to do but to cook it through and lead it to its own nature; then it is much better and whiter than the Silver coming from the mines. Therefore, always make your projection upon Jupiter for the white work <note>The "white work" or *albedo* results in silver.</note>, and upon Venus <note>Venus represents Copper.</note> for the red work <note>The "red work" or *rubedo* results in gold.</note>. For if you were to make the white projection upon Venus, it would cost much medicine—much more than upon Jupiter—for Jupiter is white of himself.

## CHAPTER XLI.

<margin>If it must be projected upon Venus, the stone ought to be less fusible than that which is projected upon Saturn or Mercury.</margin>
Know furthermore, my son, that you must prepare the stone according to the metal upon which you wish to project it. For the medicine that you wish to cast upon Venus, you must not make it as fusible as if you wished to cast it upon Saturn <note>Saturn represents Lead.</note>, Mercury <note>Quicksilver</note>, or Jupiter. You can make your medicine as fusible as you wish, for the more spirit you have fixed with it, the more fusible it becomes; and you could easily fix so much spirit with it that in the end you would retain a slimy powder, so that it would melt more easily than butter in the sun. Therefore take care, my son, that you do not make it so liquid. For if you wished to make a projection upon Mercury, you would make your projection more fusible than when you wish to make it upon Jupiter; for the matter ought to melt before your Mercury begins to ascend <note>To "ascend" means to vaporize or sublimate; the Stone must melt and "fix" the Mercury before the Mercury boils away.</note>. Truly, that is not necessary upon Jupiter. And whatever you do, see that you first vivify <note>To "vivify" or bring to life; in this context, preparing the base metal to be receptive to the Stone.</note> your dead body and give it a soul before you cast the medicine upon it; otherwise, your medicine would perform no projection, even if you had the most excellent medicine that ever existed in the world.

### CHAPTER XLII.

<margin>The body must be revived before projection can be made upon it.</margin>
You shall know, my son, that it is just as necessary to infuse life into a dead body <note>In alchemy, "dead" metals are those in their common, base state; "reviving" them means preparing them to receive the Stone.</note> before a projection can be made upon it, as it is necessary to place the ferment into the medicine; and hold this as a secret. *Morienus <note>Morienus Romanus was a legendary 7th-century alchemist, said to be the teacher of the Umayyad prince Khalid ibn Yazid.</note> says: Our orichalcum <note>original: "orialchalcum"; historically a gold-colored alloy like brass, but here referring to a specialized alchemical substance.</note> is not common orichalcum, for it lives and possesses a soul.*

### CHAPTER XLIII.

Furthermore, my son, you shall know that if you wish to make a projection for the Red <note>The "Red" refers to the Elixir for turning metals into Gold; the "White" is for Silver.</note> upon Venus <note>original: "Venerem"; the alchemical name for Copper.</note>, you shall always sublime and fix the matter with a low fire, however long that time may be. For when one works with a low fire, the matter better retains its humidity; and because Venus is exceedingly dry, the medicine ought to be more humid than if you were projecting it onto Saturn <note>original: "Saturnum"; the alchemical name for Lead.</note>, for Venus flows with difficulty because of its dryness. However, when you wish to make a projection onto bodies that melt easily and quickly, such as Jupiter <note>Tin</note> and Saturn <note>Lead</note>, the matter of your Stone must be sublimed with a vehement fire, for then the humidity is consumed within itself. And when you wish to make your projection upon Mercury <note>Quicksilver</note> or the Moon <note>original: "Lunam"; the alchemical name for Silver.</note>, sublime your matter over a moderate fire; for these two endure with the medicine until all their humidity is converted into redness. Then they settle themselves into a regulus <note>A "regulus" is a button of pure metal found at the bottom of a crucible after smelting.</note>, just as the Sun <note>Gold</note> or the Moon do upon the cupel <note>original: "testa"; a shallow, porous dish used in refining precious metals.</note>. Thus, my son, you shall prepare your Medicine according to the metals upon which you wish to make the projection.

### CHAPTER XLIV.

Furthermore, if you wish to make a projection upon Venus and impure metal: take 50 or 60 lbs of Saturn or Venus, and calcine <note>To "calcine" is to reduce a metal to a powder or ash by heating it in air.</note> them, and wash them from all impurity. Then, dissolve them again into one joined body, and instill the soul, and vivify it. Once this is done, cast the Medicine upon them—not because it is strictly necessary to purge impure metals before you make a projection upon them (for indeed your medicine has the power of transforming all impure metals into the Sun and the Moon), but because once purged by calcination and washing, they lose their impurity and dryness. They melt gradually and are cleansed of combustible sulfur, so that your medicine extends itself much further than if the metals were in their state of impurity. For example: your medicine may be worth 1,000 <note>This refers to the "multiplication" or ratio—the amount of base metal one part of the Stone can transform.</note> on unpurified metal; but with metals already purged, it will easily proceed to 10,000. Thus, the labor is well compensated.

### CHAPTER XLV.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration of a tall cylindrical earthenware vessel, likely a crucible or calcining pot, with its circular lid shown separately above its opening.</image-desc>

<margin>How Venus is to be calcined.</margin>
Likewise, to calcine Venus <note>original: "Venerem"; the alchemical name for Copper.</note>, take a large, square earthenware vessel made of firm clay that does not crack, fashioned in this manner: it shall have a lid fitted to it that matches it exactly and closes it tight. Then, taking red copper, cut it into square pieces of such a size that they may lie within the vessel. Then make all those pieces red-hot in the fire and extinguish <note>This process of heating and sudden cooling is called "quenching."</note> them in old urine. Repeat this four times, heating them until they glow and always quenching them in fresh "old" urine <note>Alchemists used aged urine because the urea breaks down into ammonia, which acts as a powerful cleaning and reacting agent on the metal surface.</note>. Then wash them in clean water and wipe them clean with a linen cloth in the Sun; then your Venus is prepared for calcination. 

Then take white arsenic <note>Arsenic trioxide, a common reagent used to whiten or "fix" copper.</note> sublimated two or three times; grind it upon a stone with sharp distilled wine vinegar until it reaches the consistency of a thick paste, as if you intended to paint with it. Smear your plates with this paste and set them to dry in the Sun or in a dry bath. Then smear them again, dry them again, and repeat this a third time, coating them everywhere. When they are dry for the last time, take common salt that has been dissolved and congealed once <note>This refers to purified salt that has been recrystallized.</note>, and spread it over the bottom of the vessel until it rises to the measure of a finger's breadth. Place a layer of plates upon this; then another layer of salt, and proceed in this order until your vessel is full. 

Then place it in the furnace and apply a gentle heat, of such a temperature as the Sun has in March <note>A traditional alchemical way of describing a moderate, warming heat rather than a scorching fire.</note>. Allow the moisture to evaporate thoroughly for two or three days continuously. Then seal <note>original: "luta"; to seal a vessel with "lute," a specialized clay or paste meant to withstand high temperatures.</note> the lid upon the earthenware vessel with firm lute so that nothing can escape. When this is done, allow it to dry thoroughly so it does not crack. 

Next, place the vessel in the calcining furnace. First, apply a small fire for 12 hours so that the vessel does not glow; then you shall increase the fire gradually by degrees so that 6 or 8 hours later the vessel glows entirely. Keep it thus in that hot flame for 12 hours, then allow it to cool. Presently, break the vessel and remove all the salt by dissolving it with hot fire <note>The text likely implies using hot water aided by residual heat to wash away the salt.</note>. If the metal is not entirely calcined, proceed as before; set it to be calcined again as you did previously, except you will not need to make it red-hot or extinguish it in urine. When everything has been calcined and the salt has been thoroughly washed away, pound those ashes <note>original: "calces"; the powder (calx) remaining after a metal has been "burned" or oxidized.</note> in an iron mortar and pass them through a sieve. Once this is done, wash them again with fresh water until the water flows away clear; then dry them in a pan over the furnace, and again...

Grind it in an iron mortar and sift it through a sieve. Afterward, grind the powders <note>original: "calces"; literally "limes," referring here to the metallic ash or powder resulting from the previous treatment.</note> upon a stone with honey, mixing in a little water until they are so fine that a painter could paint with them. Then wash it again with hot water until the water runs off clean. Then dry the powders once more in a pan over the furnace as described above; thus your Copper <note>original: "Venus"</note> is clean and pure. Then take Alkali salt <note>Sal alcali: likely potassium carbonate.</note> and Glass salt <note>Sal vitri: a flux often made from the surface scum of molten glass.</note>, both ground into a powder, and mix them into the aforementioned metallic powders. <image-desc>A woodcut illustration of a 'sacculus lineus' or linen bag, used in chemical processes. It is depicted with a bulbous body and a long, narrow, curved neck that appears to be tied off at the end.</image-desc>

Fill it with the aforementioned material as tightly as you possibly can, packing it in with a wooden tool. Once it is well-stopped, tie its end firmly. Then coat the bag with lute <term>lute: a heat-resistant cement or clay used to seal vessels</term> mixed with hair <note>Alchemists added animal hair or straw to their clay "lute" to act as a binder, preventing the coating from cracking when exposed to extreme heat.</note> so that it does not split. Coat it all around and let it dry; coat it again and let it dry once more, repeating this until the coating is three fingers thick.

When the material is thoroughly dry, drill a hole in the side of one part and place it in a wind furnace <note>A furnace designed to create a strong draft of air to reach higher temperatures.</note> so that the perforated end lies half a foot lower than the other. Position a large crucible beneath the hole and build a fire under the coated bag with oak charcoal. Melt the contents so that everything flows down into the crucible, then let it cool. Afterward, melt it again; then it is ready. To ten pounds of that Copper, add one pound of cupelled Silver <note>original: "Lunae cupellatae"; silver refined using a cupel to ensure its purity.</note>. Dissolve them together, and it is ready to receive your "white medicine" <note>The "medicine" refers to the alchemical agent (often a precursor to the Philosopher's Stone) used to transform the metal.</note>.

If you wish to prepare the Copper for the "red medicine" <note>The "red medicine" or Red Work was intended for the creation of Gold, whereas the "white" was for Silver.</note>, take instead of white arsenic a good red or saffron-colored arsenic <note>Likely realgar or orpiment, which are arsenic sulfides.</note> sublimated two or three times, and rub your plates with it. Proceed as above with half vitriol and half salt, layer upon layer, and so on as described.

You shall know, my son, that this calcination is not strictly necessary in the sense that the medicine for the white or red would otherwise lack the power to transform Copper into Silver or Gold. Indeed, it possesses those powers even if the metal is not calcined in this manner. However, the medicine does not "tinge" <note>Tingeing refers to the alchemical process of deeply dyeing or permanently changing the color and nature of a metal.</note> as deeply as when the Copper is so prepared. When prepared this way, your medicine may achieve a projection ten thousand times higher than if you cast it upon unprepared Copper, which still contains "combustible sulfur" <note>Alchemists believed that base metals were "sick" because they contained an impure, flammable sulfur that caused them to tarnish or burn away; removing it was essential for a permanent transformation.</note> along with many other drosses. It is also much more pleasant to perform a projection upon a pure metal than an impure one, for upon an impure metal, the medicine must first purge the metal itself before a transformation can occur.

### CHAPTER XLVI.

Now I wish to teach the stone for the Red, and it is a greater secret, and requires more time and labor: it must be more subtle than the stone for the White <note>The "White Stone" was the version of the elixir used to create silver; the "Red Stone" was for gold.</note>. The Red must be rectified better and longer: for it has a firm and compact body and is more fixed. For this reason, a longer time is needed before its parts can be separated from one another, in order to open it and to extract the subtle spirits from it, or at least the more subtle part.

### CHAPTER XLVII.

<margin>How the Red Stone is to be prepared.</margin>
Therefore, my son, you shall take the Red Stone, and dissolve it in its red water, and precipitate it, and wash its red water with water of clouds <note>original: "aqua nubium"; likely rainwater, which alchemists considered more "spiritually" pure than well water.</note>, and dry it in the Sun or by a small fire. Then place it in a reverberatory furnace <term>reverberatory furnace: a furnace designed to reflect or "reverberate" the heat from the roof onto the material being heated</term> to be calcined for 12 or 16 days: but you must take care lest you cause the stone to flow <note>i.e., melt it prematurely.</note>. Therefore, give it a modest flame: then take it out and dissolve it again in water. Once this is done, place it in putrefaction, that is, in a warm bath <note>original: "balneo calido"; often referring to the 'balneum Mariae' or water bath.</note>, and leave it there for eight days. Then distill that water again in a lukewarm bath. Having done these things, take out the Gold <note>original: "Solem"</note>...

### CHAPTER 48.

<margin>What must be done with the aforesaid powder.</margin>

Likewise, then take out that white powder and place it to be reverberated <term>reverberated: a process of heating material in a furnace where the flames are reflected or "reverberated" off the roof onto the substance</term> in a moderate fire until it swells up completely like a sponge. If by chance any **Gold** remains in those dregs, place them to be reverberated again for two days and again attempt to dissolve them. Then you will easily be able to see whether anything further dissolves or not. Mix together everything that has been dissolved and distill the vinegar through an alembic <term>alembic: a distillation apparatus consisting of two vessels and a tube</term>, and the whitest and clearest matter will remain for you at the bottom. These thick parts have now been made "subtle" <note>refined or purified</note>; keep this in a glass vessel for use.

Then take all the colored vinegar that you drew out from the thick parts and distill the vinegar; a red powder will remain for you at the bottom, like **dragon's blood** <term>dragon's blood: a traditional name for a deep red resin, used here to describe the intense color of the alchemical precipitate</term>. Place that powder to be sublimated <term>sublimation: heating a solid until it becomes a vapor and then solidifies again on a cooler surface to purify it</term> by itself, adding nothing else. It will all sublimate into a white form. If any dregs remain, you can sublimate them afterward, but it will not be worth the effort. Therefore, take them out and throw them away, and sublimate the rest again until nothing more remains. Then it is enough; take it and keep it well.

MASTER JOHANNES ISAAC

# CHAPTER 50.

Now you may ask, my son, in what way the medicine shall be acquired which may transform **Mercury** into true **Gold** <note>original: "Solem" (the Sun)</note> or **Silver** <note>original: "Lunam" (the Moon)</note>, for it seems impossible according to the reasons previously stated.

<margin>The great secret of the Alchemical art.</margin>
Know, my son, as a great secret in the art, that the medicine for the "white" or "red" work, which in the beginning was dissolved in vinegar or common water, is always dissolved in vinegar, common water, or wine after its perfection. For when the white or red stone is perfected, it is easily 1,000 times more subtle than it was before its perfection, when it was dissolved in vinegar. For the more noble a thing is, and the more subtle its nature, the more easily it is dissolved: for no coarse parts are present, nor dregs, nor dryness, which are separated through dissolution in vinegar. For the coarse parts, dregs, and superfluous dry parts (which are as one) are the things that prevent it from being led to dissolution. But the white and red stone have none of these things within themselves: instead, they are soluble above all things that exist in the nature of things, in both—that is, in burning dryness and in cold humidity. For in them there are no parts which could hinder liquefaction; and in the whole world, there is no nature so perfect as our white and red stone. Therefore, there is nothing in the nature of things that can be dissolved in both—that is, in burning dryness and cold humidity—as our stone can.

# CHAPTER 51.

Therefore, my son, hold this as a great secret in the art: to know our stone in its interior nature; and know that no medicine, whether for the white or the red, can be prepared for the work so fusible <term>fusible: able to be melted or liquefied by heat</term> that it could retain **Mercury** over the fire, without it flying away <note>original: "subvolaret"; referring to the volatility of mercury, which evaporates before most solids melt</note> before the medicine can melt.

Furthermore, know that when you have prepared the medicine for the white or red work so that you may perform a projection <term>projection: the final stage of alchemy where the "stone" is cast upon a molten base metal to transform it</term> into hard metals and into soft bodies, and you then desire to perform a projection into **Mercury** to prove the art: take a part of your medicine for the white or the red which you have prepared, and dissolve it in sharp distilled vinegar, so rectified <term>rectified: purified by repeated distillation</term> that it leaves absolutely nothing behind itself. Congeal it again, and dissolve it repeatedly in fresh vinegar until it becomes fusible like butter. Then cease the dissolving, and cast it upon the **Mercury**, and perform the projection according to the art; you should dissolve and congeal it so many times that it grows together into an oil which would no longer wish to congeal. For in all vegetables or animals, there is no hope of such solubility as there is in wine.

### CHAPTER 53.

<margin>Everything that God created has within itself the 4 elements.</margin>
Know, my son, that everything God created has within itself the four elements, as is well taught in the *Book of Vegetables* <note>Referring to Johannes Isaac Hollandus's own "De Vegetabilibus," a work on plant-based alchemy</note>; and although the matter may appear white on the outside, on the contrary, the same matter is red inside. Therefore, the Red Stone places the whiteness of the Moon <note>Luna; alchemical code for Silver</note> inside and brings the redness out to the surface, thus reducing the Moon to the Stone’s own nature. 

Just as can be seen daily in all things born of the earth—such as apples, pears, plums, cherries, flowers, and many other fruits—when they hang upon the trees and are ripe: see what a remarkable red color they acquire from the splendor of the Sun shining directly upon them. Observe how the apple grows red on the side where the Sun shone upon it, and how the heat of the Sun has drawn the redness of the fruit outward. Therefore, my son, do not wonder that one part of the Stone can reduce a thousand parts of the Moon to its own nature. 

Furthermore, when the Sun <note>Sol; alchemical code for Gold</note> is led out of its own nature, so that it is stripped of its body <note>original: "exutus corpore"; meaning the metal is dissolved or "opened" to release its spiritual essence</note> to the point that it can no longer become a physical body, it is as red as dark blood, or like dried Dragon's Blood <note>a bright red resin from the Dracaena tree, used as a pigment and in alchemy</note> or goat’s blood; and it is so full of color that it cannot be described. For when it is dissolved and then coagulated again, the weight of a single grain of wheat would easily imbue ten *lota* <note>an old German weight, roughly half an ounce</note> of white wine with its color. Such an abundance of color resides within the Sun: therefore, do not wonder.

## Concerning the Stone from both Lights.
### CHAPTER LVI.

<margin>The preparation of the Philosophers' Stone from the two lights.</margin>
Likewise, I now wish to teach you how to prepare the **Philosophers' Stone** from the two lights <note>The "two lights" refer to the Sun (Gold) and the Moon (Silver)</note>, just as the ancient Philosophers and their successors prepared it with their own hands. I shall do so without obscurity of words, explaining its operation, its powers, and its translation from its own nature into its **First Essence** <term>First Essence (Prima Essentia): the pure, original state of a substance before it has been shaped into a specific form by nature</term>. 

For no thing can be transferred out of its own nature once Nature has completed its final operation upon it, as she has done in these two lights. For even if these two lights had lain in the mines from which they came until the Day of Judgment, Nature would have worked nothing more upon them. Nature had already exerted her ultimate power within them. Thus, if we wish to reduce these two together from their current nature into something better or worse, we must go backward. We must "unweave" <note>original: "retexendum"; meaning to dismantle the chemical structure to return it to a primitive state</note> that which Nature has worked, and reduce it into the same form it held when Nature first began to work upon it. 

Once it has been brought back to that form, we must follow Nature as closely as we can—and sometimes, Nature herself must even be surpassed. 

<margin>Nature must be followed, and also sometimes surpassed.</margin>
Specifically, this is done through separating and rectifying, dissolving and congealing, **calcination** <term>calcination: heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to a powder</term> and purification, as well as joining, waxing, and various thinning—and other works which Nature cannot perform. For Nature is not moved to perform works of this kind. Therefore, we transfer metals into another and better form than Nature made, or indeed, than she is able to make. But the two diseases of Silver—such as the "combustible sulfur," which prevents Silver from standing in the cement <note>original: "cæmento"; a refining process using heat and acid</note>, nor allows it to pass through antimony, nor retain colors—and the foul, black, "incombustible sulfur," only cling to the outside of the Silver and do not penetrate its innermost root. In this way, the combustible sulfur can be removed, as has been taught here—truly, it is not as easily removed from the other four metals as it is from Silver. The other disease by which Silver is held back is coldness and immoderate moisture, which likewise only clings to the outside of the Silver and does not penetrate the interior of its root. And therefore, these two diseases can easily be driven away from Silver, which cannot be done with the others. The first disease...

# MINERAL WORKS

...from the Moon <note>original: "Luna"; alchemists used this name for Silver</note>, namely, the combustible sulfur is removed from the Silver by calcination with arsenic and by washing, as described above. You should also know that arsenic, in its crude state, burns and consumes all bodies, as do orpiment <term>auripigmentum|a golden-yellow arsenic sulfide mineral</term> and sulfur. All three of these share the same nature, in that they burn, calcine, and destroy the bodies with which they are mixed. But when arsenic and orpiment have been freed and cleansed of their impurity, earthiness, crude spirits, and non-fixed parts, you then take the "intermediate spirit" from them. With that spirit, you drive away all combustible sulfur from the metals, as you frequently calcine, wash, grind, cleanse, and melt them with it, and then calcine them again. Repeat this as many times as necessary until they are liberated from their own combustible sulfur. For Silver, however, this must be done only once, because the sulfur only adheres to the outside of the Silver. Thus, arsenic or orpiment is similar to Theriac <note>original: "Theriaca"; a famous historical herbal jam or "treacle" used as a universal antidote</note>: for the material from which it is made can poison and kill men—as it is indeed a poison—but when that poison is prepared into Theriac, it repels all other poisons from poisoned men. Prepared arsenic and orpiment perform the same function for metals.

<margin>Another disease of Silver: superfluous coldness and humidity.</margin> Another disease of Silver is superfluous coldness and humidity, which likewise adhere to the outside of the Silver. These are removed from the Silver by calcining it in a furnace in which spirits are calcined. By this means, the Silver is reduced to a balanced temperature so that the Stone <note>The "Stone" refers to the Elixir or Philosopher's Stone being produced from the metal</note> may be extracted from it. However, it still consists of coarse and fixed parts and is "feminine" in nature. Therefore, Morienus <note>A legendary 7th-century alchemist</note> says: *Unless you cleanse the imperfect body, you will waste your labor in our art and mastery.*

...of the philosopher is perfected: What is enclosed in it, unlock; what is dry, moisten; what is moist, dry out: then seek the coldness of the Moon <note>original: "Lunae"; Silver</note>, and you will find the heat of the Sun <note>original: "Solis"; Gold</note>: and seek the heat of the Sun, and you will find the coldness of the Moon.

### CHAPTER LIX.

<margin>The material from which the stone is to be extracted is ready.</margin>
Likewise, now the material for extracting the stone is ready. You should know, therefore, that almost all the material of the Sun will ascend together, and will carry up with it all the subtle parts of the Moon: yet of the Moon, nothing or very little ascends except its subtle parts. The greatest part of the Moon is crude, cold, and feminine, and it remains at the bottom. But the Sun alone in its parts is subtle and masculine: and once the Sun is "unlocked" <note>opened or decomposed into its primary essence</note>, everything ascends together because of its great subtlety: just as the Moon remains below at the bottom, and does not wish to ascend because of its thickness <note>density or grossness of matter</note>. Thus, a contrariety exists in these two bodies; the destruction of one is the nourishment of the other. Therefore, both are necessary together in the work, as you well know. 

<margin>This material must be sublimated:</margin>
In addition, set this material to be sublimated <term>sublimation|the process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then collecting the deposit as it cools</term> by all means as has been taught in the "white and red work" <note>the two main stages of creating the Philosopher's Stone: the Albedo (white) and Rubedo (red)</note>. And you must beware of the air when you open your vessels and when you take out the spirit, for the air would kill you. Therefore, allow your vessels to cool properly before you break them open. And if it should happen by chance that the spirits penetrate your <term>lute|lutum; a clay or paste used to seal alchemical vessels against leaks</term> during sublimation, or if the <term>alembic|a distillation apparatus</term> should crack or develop fissures, or even the glass pot itself, beware of that air, for it would kill you instantly. For its air <note>the vaporous spirit of the metal</note> ascends invisibly because of its great subtlety, and the more subtle you make it, the more burning and poisonous it becomes. For God created no spirit among all mineral things more burning nor more subtle than the spirit of the Sun, nor any spirit more subtle or fleeting than the Sun. 

If the Sun were "open" in its parts as the Moon is, or as other metals are, or if the four elements which are in the Sun were contrary to one another, the Sun would ascend from the fire more easily than any mineral spirit. But the elements are so equally balanced in the Sun, and so clean and pure, that they cannot now, nor at any time, be separated. Therefore, when the Sun is unlocked, everything flies upward together, so that it leaves nothing behind, unless perhaps some other substance of other metallic things was mixed with it. For any other metallic body, or any metallic thing, easily melts together with the Sun. For everything coming from the mines willingly joins itself with the Sun and is friendly with it. For the Sun is King and Lord.

Therefore, he who wishes to complete the work from the Sun <note>original: "Sole"; Gold</note> alone must take care not to open or release the Sun so much that it is prepared like a ferment <note>a substance that triggers a transformation, like leaven in bread</note>; otherwise, the whole would ascend together, one with the other. If this should happen, a ferment of the crude powder of the Sun should be added if you are to perfect the stone; however, it would not be to your advantage to use crude ferment. But if it should happen that all your Sun ascends together, it would be more to your advantage to complete the white stone from the Moon <note>original: "Luna"; Silver</note> to the white stage, and to make it so that it cannot be melted, and then to wax <note>original: "incerare"; to treat the material to make it soft or fusible like wax</note> it with the spirit of the Sun: in this way, you would have a double benefit and profit. For you would bring the white stone to the power of the Sun, and the spirit together with the soul into its own power; a matter which will be taught in another work. You might ask then: I had thought the Sun was entirely fixed <note>stable and resistant to change by fire</note>. For it remains in the cupel <note>original: "quartale"; a small shallow vessel used in assaying gold</note> without loss, and also in the cement, in antimony, and in the fire. For even if the Sun were to lie in the fire forever, the Sun would not be consumed in the fire: and if the Sun lay under the earth until the end of the world, it would not be corrupted or putrefied.

<margin>The Sun cannot be corrupted by anything.</margin>
By no things that are in the world can the Sun be corrupted. For the Sun is simple, and all its parts and its elements are not contrary to each other: its oil and its salt are so joined with the four elements: and its Mercury and its sulfur are so firmly mixed into one with its oil and salt, in such a combination with the four elements, that they are of the same nature; and the parts are equal on both sides: so that the Sun is only one thing; and being a single thing, which is no longer made of other things, it cannot be separated from itself by any means. Such is the Sun, for it is nothing but one single thing.

### CHAPTER LX.

Likewise, against the odor or the air <note>the toxic fumes</note> of the stone when you sublimate it, bind two glass eyes <note>protective goggles</note> before your eyes, and a wide piece of leather before the mouth and nostrils; into this leather, a double wool cloth should be inserted, and over that wool cloth a wide sponge, and bind it before the mouth and nostrils: in this you will be able to breathe: and guard yourself against the air, for it ascends invisibly.

<margin>The body is to be dissolved with vinegar. It is to be congealed and reverberated <note>heated in a furnace where the flame is reflected back onto the substance</note>. It is to be dissolved again in vinegar. Then reverberated again for 5 or 6 hours. Again dissolved in common water and congealed. Dissolved again in common water. Congealed again.</margin>

What we have called "dregs" <note>original: "fæces"</note> is the body of the Moon <note>Silver</note>, which even now lies buried in the dregs; for as yet not much of the Moon has ascended <note>risen or sublimated</note>, which is the body and the ferment <note>the substance that triggers the alchemical transformation</note> of our stone. Thus, dissolve the body from the dregs with distilled vinegar—whatever part of it is willing to be dissolved. Then congeal it, and then set it to be reverberated for 24 hours with a gentle fire, until it truly glows with a reddish color, and no more; let it cool. Then take it out and dissolve it again in distilled vinegar. Then congeal it anew. Then set it again to be reverberated for 5 or 6 hours, until it truly glows and no more; let it cool, take it out, and once more dissolve it in common water, and congeal it again. After this, make it glow until it truly reddens for the duration of 5 or 6 Lord's Prayers <note>original: "orationum dominicarum"; a common medieval method for timing laboratory processes by reciting prayers</note>. Then take it out again, and dissolve it anew in common water distilled so many times that nothing remains. You shall repeat this dissolving until you leave behind no more dregs, but the water flows from it so clear that nothing more can be seen in it, as if nothing had been dissolved in it at all. Then congeal it again until almost all the moisture has been distilled away; then let it cool. Once cooled, the material will crystallize into large pieces <note>original: "lapillaret"</note>, the length and thickness of fingers, bright like clear crystal, and white in the manner of snow. Then evaporate these fragments until they become a fine powder, white as snow. This entire operation must be carried out in glass bowls prepared for this purpose, standing over a boiling water bath <note>original: "balneo bulliente"</note>, with the vessels covered with a double linen cloth so that no dust or dirt flies in. For our work must be clean and extremely pure. And then the precious earth—both the body and the ferment—is prepared to receive the soul and the spirit into them, and to embrace them with great friendship and great desire, so that they may remain together forever in great concord and peace; so that hereafter they may never be separated at any time; and they shall reign forever with great subtlety and power. For the body desires to receive its own soul and spirit; and the soul with the spirit desires to descend and rest in its own body. For one cannot exist without the other. And when they have been joined together as is fitting, there is such a firm bond of love between them that they unite entirely and are mixed one with the other, so that they become of the same nature and one single thing. And then the matter is simple, like the invincible heaven; and thus it is the Quintessence <note>the "fifth essence," a purified state of matter beyond the four elements</note> for healing all diseases in an instant.
