# THE FIRST WHEEL OF THE GOLDEN CHARIOTS, A TREATISE ON THE

## PHILOSOPHY OF METALS
->*written by a most learned and experienced anonymous man.*<-

### On Gold.

<note>The woodcut initial 'S' at the beginning of "SOL" depicts a figure or floral motifs, common in late 16th-century printing to signal the start of a major chapter.</note>

SOL <note>original: "SOL." In alchemy, Sol (the Sun) is the universal symbol for gold.</note>, the prince of the other metals, becomes entirely purified through its most perfect decoction <note>original: "decoctionem." This refers to the process of refining or "cooking" a substance over heat until it reaches maturity.</note>. This is proven by the dryness of its pores and its sound, which falls between sharp and deep. It glows scarlet in the fire, and although examined a thousand times, it richly preserves its consistency and its weight. It is befriended by quicksilver <note>original: "argēto viuo." Literally "living silver," known to us as Mercury.</note> more than the other metals; this embrace is caused not only because it is part of its nature, but because of the appetite between the dry and the moist. It possesses a salt, which is its glue. From this salt is made an oil, which they call the "sulphur of the philosophers." If you dissolve it into a lime <note>original: "calcē." A calx is the crumbly powder resulting from the oxidation of a metal through heat.</note>, it possesses a fire through which it happens that it mixes with nothing else; for there is no proportion between it and the rest. Its substance is its spirit, but a body happens to it when it is held in salt. From its very beginning, however, its spirit possesses this; and it happens that it communicates with all metals, but especially and more purely with copper <note>original: "ære." In this context, likely refers to copper or bronze used in alloying.</note>, as is clear to the eye in dissolutions. Nor should you be ignorant that a flower is produced from the boiled blood of Mercury <note>original: "sanguine Mercurij." A metaphorical term for a specific stage of the alchemical process or a specific reagent.</note>, the fruit of which is the spirit of gold.

Unless you apply the mind of understanding to my mouth, studious seeker <note>original: "speculator." Literally an observer or investigator.</note>, you will labor in vain. For it is necessary for you to thoroughly search out and understand what you are finally going to do, and to diligently and deeply direct every word of this primary discourse. For I do not reveal these things through the parables and enigmas that I have seen and proved by experiment, but with the open proofs of science; if you do not grasp these with a sound mind, do not sweat further. Neither is this enough, unless the divine goodness supports you.

Mercury and sulphur, by coming together like male and female, bring about generation not only in metals, but truly also in precious stones. Sulphur is indeed abundantly fiery and dry, while Mercury is moist. In the womb of the earth and the matrix of the water they conceive, and from the conjunction of both there is made—as if from seed—a fetus or embryo, which is gradually nourished by the purity of the Mercury,

### *On the imitation of nature by art.*

What is perfected within the earth can be perfected through art <note>In this context, "Art" refers to the practice of Alchemy—the human technological imitation of natural processes.</note> by the movement of time. I will teach you the method of this, and in the shortest time, if you do not fail. Take from the refined gifts of nature a male and a female, and join them in their own kind, with the mother nourishing them as at first and the father, sulphur, providing warmth; and you will have the desired corporeal spirit, which turns its mother and brothers into itself—and this is achieved by various means and methods tending toward this goal.

### *On the Moon.*

<note>original: "De Luna." In alchemy, Luna (the Moon) is the universal symbol for silver.</note>

Let us follow the nature of the Moon, which is both the sister and the spouse of the Sun; it is conceived and born in a similar way through much decoction <note>original: "decoctione." The process of "cooking" or maturing a substance through heat.</note>. However, it cannot become "white gold"; rather, when it is nourished by a heat that is not quite so perfect, silver is produced, and a defect proceeds from the womb. This is understood from the association with tin <note>original: "stagni." Tin was often found near silver and was considered a "diseased" or "immature" form of the metal.</note> joined to it in the silver mines. When the vessel is more porous or otherwise open, the original spirit exhales and evaporates the Mercury; this happens because the heat fails and becomes weaker than it ought to be. Its substance is its spirit, just as was said of the Sun: it catches fire and is resonant, because its natural moisture has been dried out within it. Therefore it is white, with a whiteness tending toward redness, because the moisture has been removed; for if it had been cooked more, the fire would have made an impression upon it, just as the heat of the Sun stamps a color upon fruits after their whiteness. The redness indicates the loss of its moisture, signifying the command of the dominant heat; and if it is joined together, there occurs in it a serenity, which is the foundation of whiteness, just as whiteness is the foundation of redness. For this reason, a celestial color <note>Likely referring to a blue or azure tint.</note> is made from the Moon, if the spirit—and not the liquid—enters through the pores of the moisture; and that color is more "salty," from which precious stones descend. However, the blackness which is in the Moon denotes its change/decay; just as the azure color of silver appears in copper...

### *On Tin.*

Tin is a soft metal, inconsistent, and not enduring the fire <note>original: "ignitionem non patiens." Tin has a notably low melting point compared to other metals.</note>. Nature intended to produce Gold, or at least to produce Silver <note>original: "Lunam."</note>; certain gold and silver lines appearing within it prove this conception: but due to a defect in the vessel <note>The "vessel" here refers to the earth or the specific geological pocket where the metal formed.</note>, and the impurity of the paternal substance <note>In the "mercury-sulfur theory," sulfur is the active male principle or "father" and mercury is the "mother."</note>, the heat failed, and thus it did not receive the digested nourishment of its parents. For this reason, you see in it a certain blackish whiteness, from a spotted and un-evaporated moisture. You also perceive a sign of its raw state in its hoarse sound and its "screeching" when in a thin plate <note>Known as the "tin cry," a distinct crackling sound made when bending a piece of tin.</note>: for this reason, it does not withstand the judgment <note>Testing by fire or "cupellation."</note>, because that moisture, not being dried out, flies away, dragging with it whatever belongs to the mother, while the paternal part remains, as is proven by experiment. The substance of Jupiter <note>Tin is traditionally associated with the planet Jupiter.</note> is a spirit not fixed, composed of the spoils of dissolvable parents and an undigested bond, yet it is malleable due to the viscosity of its salt. Furthermore, there occurs *ceruse* <note>White lead, often used as a pigment.</note>, which is the "flower of whiteness," just as red lead <note>original: "minium."</note> is in lead; from these, precious stones are made by nature and art working together. It also possesses a salt that equals the snow, from which comes an oil that stands above the fire, the power of which is marvelous in the work of his mastery.

### *On Lead.*

Hermes, Geber, and Raymond <note>Hermes Trismegistus, Geber (Jabir ibn Hayyan), and Raymond Lull—the foundational legendary and historical authorities of medieval alchemy.</note> tell marvelous things about it, asserting that it is their "hidden gold." But I will open to you what the philosophers meant: for now it is enough for you to know the cause of its redness, which is the same as that which I brought forward regarding the cause of whiteness in tin. It is, however, heavy and sweeter, and its salt is like a Topaz, from which and out of which is made a noble oil for precious stones.

### *On Copper.*

Copper <note>original: "Æs." This can refer to copper, bronze, or brass.</note> is from the same conception, but due to a defect of the vessel from which the heat vanishes, it is not "cooked" to perfection. But it could be asked: if the same reasoning applies to the conception of all, why is there such diversity in the metals? This reason is assigned: because the sulfur has not been cooked and remains mixed with the Mercury. The proof of this is the greenness <note>Verdigris, the green pigment that forms on weathered copper.</note> that is always shed by copper: whereas in Silver <note>original: "Luna."</note> it is more thoroughly cooked than in copper. Now, the first degree of moisture is blackness; the second is greenness, as is seen in Silver and Venus <note>Copper is traditionally associated with the planet Venus.</note>.

# THE GOLDEN CHARIOTS

Yet, there are preserved in Venus <note>original: "Venere." The alchemical name for Copper.</note> filaments of conception, which are the spirit of gold collected from copper; it is more noble here than in gold itself, because it is more perfectly completed in the moisture of sulfur than in gold. However, it is collected with difficulty, since it possesses no greater coherence than the air itself; indeed, it has no subject in the other substantial parts of copper. There is also in it a certain part of the Moon <note>original: "Lunæ." The alchemical name for Silver.</note>, which is collected during its dissolution around the glass, like the skin of an egg, which is the purest silver. It holds the same place as white lead <note>original: "cerusæ."</note>, from which salt and oil are made; by adding the spirit of gold to these, an Elixir is made for tinting Silver, and even a more noble Elixir—the Emerald stone—is prepared.

#### On Iron.

Iron is conceived from burnt sulfur in the Mercurial womb, yet it is not proportionally "cooked" <note>original: "decoctum." Refers to the alchemical process of maturation within the earth.</note> because nourishment from its mother was lacking; for after conception, the substance of Mercury was not present, but it was nourished by sulfur itself. The proof of this is the difficulty of its melting and the "scumming" of its saffron <note>original: "croci." Here referring to Saffron of Mars, or iron oxide/rust.</note>, which, if it were not burned away even a little, would devour the whole iron; and the scabby sparking of iron is a sign of much sulfur and little Mercury. A sweetness comes to it from prepared hartshorn <note>original: "cornu ceruino." Calcined deer antler was often used as a flux or purifying agent.</note>, so that a wire can be drawn from it. From this same source, the saffron is obtained, from which a Mercury of great value is made for the perfection of the precious stone, and especially the Diamond; also, a tinting oil is made from it. More on all these things gradually.

### *On the nature of the two spirits of metals, Sulfur and Mercury, from which precious stones also proceed; and first, on Sulfur.*

Sulfur is the spirit of generative nature, acting in a moisture suitable to itself, with the appropriate and tempered fuel of the Sun <note>Gold or celestial heat.</note> or fire. Its substance is incombustible, standing firm over the fire and "tinting" its children. This definition is far removed from that physical, combustible, and foul-smelling sulfur that defiles all metals and produces a nature contrary to them. This external sulfur, however, is suited only for fuel.

#### On Mercury.

Mercury is the wife of sulfur, receiving from him the impregnation of the fetus, since her moisture is proper for the procreation of metals and for mutual conception within her womb. Wonder...

A volatile ammonium salt used in alchemy.</note>, atraments <note>original: "atramenta." *On solutions and conjunctions.*

Dissolution and conjunction happen in metals just as they do in animals through the coitus of male and female, in the mother’s womb and the father’s bed-chamber. Sol <note>original: "Sol." The Sun, representing gold or the masculine principle.</note> and Luna <note>original: "Luna." The Moon, representing silver or the feminine principle.</note> come together well; in their union they putrefy, and in that decay they generate; from the seed comes the flower, and from the flower the fruit. This fruit converts Mercury into a thousand thousand-fold, and heals the sick, performing wonders in man. If you do not know these solutions and conjunctions, and how you should rule them, learn from the farmers who sow wheat.

*On iron and copper.*

There is no other fitting conjunction of copper <note>original: "æris." Can refer to copper, bronze, or brass.</note>, but conjunction does not happen without dissolution, and vice-versa; and so in the same way they generate, conceive, and nourish the offspring; provided, however, that the nourishment is of a more noble species.

*On tin and lead.*

Lead is the male, while tin is the female; and they are dissolved in a similar way, and their fruits are likewise dissolved and conjoined, and they become powerful for every mastery <note>original: "magisterium." The successful completion of an alchemical process.</note>.

*On many other things, which are procreated from similar material.*

Red and white coral, since they are of a metallic species, as are gold and silver marcasite <note>original: "marchasita." Usually refers to iron pyrite or similar "fool's gold" minerals.</note>, and other precious stones—if you are able to know the fitting mixtures, you will make from them a wondrous Elixir, because they are born naturally suited to make a generation more noble than themselves.

## On the transmutations of metals.

*On the Moon, that it may become the Sun.*

This is the first step for the Moon <note>Silver</note> to become the Sun <note>Gold</note>: if you place it with oil of sulfur, which is the "restraint of fugitives" <note>original: "retinaculum fugitiuorum." A substance used to "fix" or stabilize volatile chemicals.</note>, in a well-sealed glass vessel with the ferment of the Sun (which we shall teach), along with loadstone <note>original: "calamita." A natural magnet.</note> and storax <note>A fragrant plant resin.</note> for a month, cooked with a lamp striking from below, using a prepared furnace so that the color does not vanish. For there the Moon will grow heavy, grow sweet, and receive the color of the Sun within its whole substance.

### Concerning Mars <note>Iron</note>.

**I**ron, if it is sweetened, is arranged in a hartshorn <note>The antler of a stag, often used in alchemy as a source of ammonia or calcium.</note> with the ferment of the Moon <note>Silver</note>, according to the Moon. The practice of this business consists in the decoction <note>The process of boiling down</note> of it in its own water, because of the burnt sulfur that is within it, which makes for a difficult dissolution. In water, the combustion of sulfur becomes moist, whence it receives sweetness and fusion, and it receives ferment more easily than the other metals.

### Concerning Copper <note>original: "ære." Also refers to bronze or brass.</note>.

**C**opper has two of the four qualities of the Moon <note>Silver</note>: sweetness and ignition; but it lacks color and consistency. To convert it into the Sun <note>Gold</note> or the Moon <note>Silver</note>, you must first make it stand firm <note>Stabilize or "fix" the metal so it does not vaporize.</note>; then, through hidden heating, convert its greenness into whiteness, just as is done with herbs. The practice is that you add to its consistency some of the viscosity <note>original: "visco." A sticky or glutinous substance.</note> of the metal itself, which is made from its salt, and it will remain firm in the greenness of its surface; nor will it ever fly apart by means of black lead <note>Lead, associated with the planet Saturn.</note>, which is therefore at the head.

### Concerning Lead.

**C**ook lead in a reverberatory furnace <note>A furnace that reflects or "reverberates" heat onto the material from the roof, rather than applying flame directly.</note>, and when it begins to turn red, imbue it with the ferment of gold, and turn it with an iron rod; soak it little by little and drop by drop. Then, have the juice of sea purslane, soapwort, and honesty <note>original: "Lunaria." A plant with moon-shaped seed pods, highly prized in herbal alchemy.</note>; pour it over, and it will be the best and most shining gold. This is a great thing, and an exceptional secret above all others.

### Concerning Tin.

**T**in is converted into the Moon <note>Silver</note> if you place it in the furnace in the same way, ferment it, and pour over it the aforementioned juice. Likewise, if you cook it with the oil of the Moon <note>Silver</note>, sulfur, and white lead <note>original: "cerusa." Lead carbonate, a white pigment.</note> for a month—which makes a wonderful mixture—you will have the best Silver. Likewise, if you pour the water of Talc and the Moon over it in a furnace of high color, you will have the best Silver.

### Concerning the Oil of Sulfur.

**O**il of sulfur is made with the first water of metals, by a gentle uterine heat <note>original: "calor vterinus." A low, steady, moist heat likened to the temperature inside a womb.</note>, in a closed belly <note>The "ventre" or belly of a flask or vessel.</note> through a day and a night. And you will see the oil floating on top like an incombustible liquid of distilled gold. And this is the true substance and form of living sulfur; I will tell you nothing more on this matter, for this is a secret.

### *Concerning the water of Talc and of the Moon <note>Silver</note>*

The water of Talc and of the Moon <note>Silver</note> is produced in a "horse's belly" <note>original: "ventre equi." An alchemical term for a heap of fermenting horse manure, used as a source of gentle, steady heat.</note>, **from their calcined powders** <note>Powders reduced to ash through high heat</note> over nine days, and they are prepared as a mixture. If you know how to calcine them, you shall be wealthy. And this water of Talc and of the Moon is worth more than the finest pure gold <note>original: "aurum obryzon."</note>, because it beautifies the faces of women to the highest degree of brilliance.

### *Concerning pearls.*

Pearls are made from the aforementioned water, mixed with ceruse <note>White lead, commonly used in historical cosmetics</note> in the manner of pills, and cooked in the juice of the apples of the Hesperides <note>original: "Hesperidum malorum." Usually refers to citrus fruits like lemons or oranges.</note>, if they are digested in the "throat of pigeons." <note>original: "gutture columbarum." Likely a reference to a specific type of long-necked alchemical flask or a metaphor for a specific degree of gentle heat.</note>

Since some years ago certain philosophical axioms were brought to light by Bernard Penot of Port-Sainte-Marie, Doctor of Medicine—my honored friend—collected from the book of the *Twelve Gates* by George Ripley, the most learned English philosopher; and since I have discovered that certain things, greatly pertaining to the matter, were lacking in them: I considered it a worthwhile task to dedicate the entire book of that author (which has long lain hidden with me) with the appropriate faithfulness and respect to your name. For you easily hold the first rank among all philosophers in the Kingdom of England, to say nothing of other kingdoms. I wished to hand it over to the press and publish it, safe under your protection <note>original: "clypeo," literally "shield."</note>. Therefore, I have established this book as the second wheel in this <term>QUADRIGA</term> <note>A four-horse chariot. Here, it refers to Barnaud’s collection of four distinct alchemical works.</note>, so that those who wish may read the first wheel, which I placed before it (which explains in a few words the origin of metals, their mutual meeting, and their silent powers), and find in this present book the entire work, carefully repeated more than once and arranged in order. Receive therefore, most Noble man, Magnificent Lord, this work—not mine but an English one, if not to say Angelic and philosophical—with your usual gracious hand. Fare you well, most distinguished Lord, for a long and happy time, and continue to love me, your most devoted servant. At Leiden <note>original: "Lugduni Batavorum."</note>, the 15th day of July, 1599.

->*The most devoted servant of your most ample Magnificence,*<-
->NICOLAUS BARNAUD.<-

### Prologue of the Book itself.

> O incomprehensible Light, glorious in majesty, the brightness of whose rays dims our eyes. O Unity in substance, and threefold in Deity, the joyful glorification of the jubilee hierarchy. O merciful purification of souls and pure preservation, you who kindly snatch us from the occurring dangers of this turbulent valley of vanity and bring us into heaven. O power and wisdom, O inexplicable kindness, sustain me daily, and be my guide, so that my life may never displease you, but rather that I may obey you as a faithful professor <note>original: "professor." In this context, it refers to one who has taken a "profession" or religious vow, rather than a modern academic.</note>. In my beginning (good God) hear my prayers, and by the power of your grace increase my will: grant at the same time that I may be able to fulfill your will. O excellent shrine <note>original: "scrinium." A chest or casket for keeping books or valuables.</note> abounding in every treasure, you are the one from whom all goodness flows most generously to men, and to every creature. Deign therefore to protect the work of your powerful right hand, lest we waste our time in life uselessly. Grant without deceit, that we may provide for our livelihood, lest we fall into the great danger of sins. And since for your sake we have renounced our own will, the world, and its lusts, receive me as your own and willing professor: since our whole trust depends on you alone, we can do no more; we must submit ourselves to you. Deign to reveal your hidden treasures to us. Show us your secrets, and be kind to us. Among others who have professed you, I offer myself with humble submission, praying that I may be your servant, with an upright life not foreign to my profession <note>His status as a monk</note> of the order of Canons Regular of Bridlington <note>original: "Brittlintonensis." Bridlington Priory in Yorkshire was a significant Augustinian monastery where Ripley served as a canon.</note>. I beseech you, Lord, that you would deign to forgive me, for the sake of your faithful servants, if I shall reveal your secrets <note>Ripley here expresses the common alchemical anxiety that revealing the "secrets of nature" might be a transgression against God's will.</note>.

# SECOND WHEEL

In the beginning, when you created all things from nothing, a spherical and dark work was fashioned from confused chaos with you as the author—not without a miracle—containing within itself all things mixed together, which was then separated in the space of six days, as Genesis clearly testifies. Then heaven and earth were made by your word, your will, and your power; from one confused mass all things that now exist were created. But previously you were as the creator in glory, now you are, and you will be without end beyond doubt; and purified souls shall come upward to your blessedness. This beginning can serve as a declaration of our blessed stone <term>blessed stone: the Philosophers' Stone (lapis benedictus), the goal of the alchemical work</term>. For just as all things were created from one mass, so in our practice this very thing must be: for all our secrets arise from one image. In the books of the philosophers, if anyone wishes to see, our stone is called the Microcosm <note>original: "Microcosmus," meaning "little world," referring to the human being or the stone as a miniature reflection of the universe.</note>, one and three, Magnesia <note>An alchemical term for the "primordial matter" or base substance, not the modern element magnesium.</note>, and even sulfur and Mercury proportioned by nature.

But some wonder, and not without cause, and are astonished by such a wonderful thing, asking what our stone might be, since the philosophers say to those who perpetually seek it that birds and fish bring it to us, and that every one of us has it, and it is in any place, in you, in me, in every thing, time, and space. To this I respond that this is indeed Mercury, but not the common kind; it is called by the name "quicksilver" <note>original: "argentum vivum"</note>, but it is the true Mercury without which no existing thing can be. All philosophers record and say this very thing: wherefore those ignorant of philosophy undeservedly accuse us, claiming that we hide this substance; but they themselves are more to be blamed, who, though unlearned, nevertheless involve themselves in philosophy. Therefore, unless you rightly know our Mercury, in what it consists, and where you ought to seek it, beware of taking this work into your hands: for philosophers delude fools with smooth words. But if you listen to me, I will truly teach you which Mercury is most useful to you, nor will I hide anything from you in this matter.

It is found more closely in some things than in others; mark well therefore what I write to you, for if you never arrive at the knowledge of it, you shall not blame me. I will indeed teach you, so that you understand there are three Mercuries, which are the keys of the science, which Raymond <note>Likely referring to Raymond Lully, a famous medieval philosopher and alchemist.</note> calls his "menstrua" <term>menstrua: alchemical solvents or base fluids used to dissolve and transform substances</term> without which nothing is done rightly: but two of these are superficial; the third is the essential Mercury of the Sun and Moon <note>In alchemical symbolism, the Sun (Sol) represents Gold and the Moon (Luna) represents Silver.</note>, whose properties [I will describe] to you...

# THE GOLDEN CHARIOTS

I will declare it sincerely: the essential Mercury of other metals is the primary material of our stone. In our **Sun** and **Moon** <note>original: "Sole & Luna"; refers to Gold and Silver</note>, our <term>menstrua: the alchemical solvents, named after the lunar cycle (menstruum), believed to dissolve solid matter into its primal form</term> are not visible to the sight, nor do they appear except by their effect. This is that stone which we understand, if anyone reads our writings correctly. It is the soul and splendid substance of the Sun and the Moon, and their subtle influence through which the earth receives its luster. For what else are gold and silver, says <term>Avicenna: a Latinized name for Ibn Sina, a Persian polymath whose works on medicine and minerals were foundational to medieval alchemy</term>, than clean white and red earth? Take away that aforementioned luster, and the earth would be of little value. We call the whole compound our <term>plumbum: "our lead," referring not to common lead, but to the base, heavy material at the start of the Great Work</term>. The quality of the luster proceeds from the Sun and the Moon, and in short, these are our solvents.

We naturally calcine perfect bodies with the first [solvent]; but no unclean body enters except one, which is commonly called by philosophers the <term>Leo viridis: "Green Lion," a symbolic term for a potent acidic solvent or a specific state of ore that can "devour" metals</term>. This is the means of joining the tinctures between the Sun and the Moon with perfection, as <term>Geber: the Latinized name for Jabir ibn Hayyan, a legendary figure in alchemy known for his systematic approach to chemistry</term> himself testifies. With the second [solvent], which is a vegetable humidity reviving that which was previously dead, both the material and formal principles must be dissolved, otherwise they would be of little importance. Therefore, I tell you, you must know these solvents, without which neither true calcination nor natural dissolution can be performed. With the third [solvent], which is an extremely permanent humidity—incombustible and oily in its nature—the <term>Hermetis arbor: "Tree of Hermes," a symbol for the metallic structure that "grows" and branches out inside the alchemist’s flask</term> is burned into ashes. This is our most certain natural fire, our **Mercury**, our **Sulfur**, our clean tincture, our soul, our stone raised with the wind and generated in the earth. Store these things in your mind. This stone, I dare tell you, is the potential vapor of the metal; you must be cautious in how you acquire it: for indeed this solvent is invisible, although with the second **philosophical water** <note>original: "aqua philosophica"</note>, through the separation of the elements, it can appear to the sight in the form of clear water. From this solvent, brought forth by labor, the **sulfur of nature** can be made, if it be naturally sharpened and circulated into a pure spirit. Then, with it, you will be able to dissolve your base or mass in various ways, just as you will understand from practice; I will therefore declare this in its proper place along with many other things, if God grants me space and grace, and if He preserves my life in health. As I shall teach you, see that you do so, and for your first principal foundation, see that you understand your menstrual waters:

### lll 5

And now, once the **calcination** <note>original: "calcinatione"; the process of reducing a solid to a powder through high heat</note> has been completed, you must increase—rather than diminish—the **radical moisture** <note>original: "humidum radicale"; the essential, life-sustaining fluid within matter</note> until your mass, through frequent refinement, flows as easily as wax upon metal. Then, dissolve it with your **vegetable solvent** <note>original: "vegetabili menstruo"; a living, life-giving solvent rather than a corrosive mineral acid</note> until you possess an oil of a clear color; then that solvent will be visible to the sight. A gold-colored oil—or something similar—is extracted from our subtle **red lead** <note>original: "rubro plumbo"; not common lead, but the heavy, "ennobled" base material of the Work</note>. **Raymond** <note>Raymond Lully (c. 1232–1315), a legendary alchemist and philosopher</note> said, when he was an old man, that this was worth far more than common gold. For when he was near death due to his great age, he made **potable gold** <note>original: "aurum potabile"; an alchemical elixir of liquid gold believed to cure all diseases and prolong life</note> from it, which revived him.

Indeed, that oil and the vegetable solvent can be **circulated** <note>original: "circulari"; to be distilled repeatedly in a closed vessel so the vapor returns to the liquid</note> together, and thus through art and labor be made to overflow, becoming through the Art the **celestial stone**. It is of such a fiery nature that we call it our **basilisk** <term>basilisk: a mythical serpent-king whose gaze was fatal; here, it refers to a substance so potent it instantly "kills" or solidifies liquid mercury</term> and a great **Elixir** of immense value. Just as the gaze of the basilisk kills whatever it looks upon, so this stone "kills" crude **Mercury** when it is cast upon it in the blink of an eye. It does this so quickly that the Mercury perfectly **tinctures** <note>original: "tingat"; stains or transforms the inner nature</note> all bodies into the **Sun** and **Moon** <note>Gold and Silver</note> with a stable dye. In this way, govern both your red and white bases. 

Potable gold is made in this manner from gold—not gold calcined by common methods, but from our **tincture** which does not vanish, extracted from our base with the circulated solvent. Nevertheless, a natural refinement must occur before your gold is dissolved; consider this principle to be told to you above all things.

***

Now I wish to divide this treatise into **twelve chapters** <note>Though the author states twelve, only ten are listed on this page</note>. With proper summary, and setting aside unnecessary repetitions, I study only to give true information on both the theory and the practice of the operation, so that whoever wishes to be taught by my writings may perfectly achieve their purpose.

1.  The first chapter will treat **natural calcination**.
2.  The second, **secret and philosophical dissolution**.
3.  The third, our **elemental separation**.
4.  The fourth, **matrimonial conjunction**.
5.  The fifth, **putrefaction** shall follow.
6.  The sixth will be concerning **whitening congelation**.
7.  The seventh, **cibation** <note>original: "cibatione"; the "feeding" of the stone with new material to increase its strength</note> shall follow.
8.  The eighth shall demonstrate the secret of our **sublimation**.
9.  The ninth shall be concerning **fermentation**.
10. In the tenth, I shall deal with **true exaltation** in a few words.

### *Concerning calcination, with the preservation of the innate heat and the radical moisture. The First Gate.*

**CALCINATION** <note>original: "CALCINATIO"; usually the reduction of a solid to powder by heat, but here a specialized alchemical refinement</note> is the purification of our stone, restoring it with its own natural heat, so that nothing of the **radical moisture** <note>original: "radicali humido"; the essential, life-sustaining fluid within matter</note> is lost, bringing about the **solution** <note>original: "solutionem"; the process of turning a solid into a liquid state</note> primarily necessary for our stone. I admonish you to imitate the Philosophers; do not work in the common manner, with sulfurs or salts prepared in various ways. For our stone is not calcined by corrosives, nor by fire alone, nor by vinegar, nor by **burning waters** <note>original: "aquis ardentibus"; strong acids or distilled alcohols</note>, nor by the vapor of lead, according to our purpose. Whoever strives to calcine in this way, pull back your hand from this difficult science until you understand our calcination better. For by this kind of calcination, bodies are destroyed, which diminishes the moisture of our stone: for when bodies are burnt into a dry powder, like ashes or burnt bones, we do not want this kind of calcination at all: for we multiply the radical moisture in calcination, diminishing nothing of it. And for the foundation of our calcination, work cautiously, **like with like** <note>original: "genus cum genere"; the principle that substances must be of the same nature to combine effectively</note> only: for like with like has a desirable inclination. He who does not know this is blind in the science. He may wander like a mist driven by the winds, uncertain where he might find some benefit, because he cannot rightly understand our words.

<margin>—</margin>Join like with like, and species with species, as is proper. For every sprout corresponds to its own seed; man generates man, beast generates beast. <margin>—</margin>Truly, it is not very necessary to treat this more broadly, but observe one thing here if you wish to obtain the goal: every **spirit is fixed** <term>fixed: the process of making a volatile substance stable and resistant to fire</term> by the **calces** <note>original: "calcibus"; the powders produced by calcination</note> of its own kind. Having noted this well, you will bear fruit. <margin>—</margin>And we make an **unctuous calx** <note>original: "calcem... vnctuosam"; a "fatty" or oily powder that remains moist and meltable, unlike common dry ash</note>, both white and red of three degrees, before our base is perfect, liquid like wax: otherwise it is of no use, and this through a long process, as the philosophers write: for we take a year, and more, according to our expectation, <margin>—</margin>for in a shorter span of time our calx cannot be made capable of **fusion** <note>original: "fusionis"; the ability to melt or flow</note>, with a color that does not vanish. Concerning the proportion, you must pay attention, for many are deceived in this; therefore, lest you ruin your work, let your bodies be subtili-

Therefore, first perform the rotation of your elements, and turn earth into water before all else; then from water make air through refinement <note>original: "levigationem"; the process of grinding a substance into a fine powder or smoothing it out, often using liquid</note>, and reduce air into fire; then I shall call you a master of our whole mastery <note>original: "magisterij"; the "Magistery" or Great Work of creating the Philosopher's Stone</note>, both the great and the small, for you have turned the wheel of the elements, correctly understanding our writings. Once this is accomplished, turn your wheel backward, and convert fire into water, and air into earth, otherwise you labor in vain. Therefore, under the moisture of the Moon and under the tempered heat of the Sun, let your elements be quickly incinerated, and then you have attained the whole mastery. Then give thanks to God that your work has begun, for in this you have a true sign, which will appear to you in blackness. We call this sign the Raven’s Head <note>original: "Corui caput"; the hallmark of the 'Nigredo' stage, signaling the death/putrefaction of the old matter</note>; some name this the Raven’s Beak, some call it the ashes of the tree of Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note>, and thus they name it according to their own judgment; some call it our toad, which is fed from the earth, through which it is mortified: a spirit intoxicated or infected with poison. But it has almost infinite names, for it is named after every thing that is black in appearance, until it begins to grow white. For after the blackness, when it becomes bright, then it has more pleasant names, according to white things, and similarly red ones; thus it has its own designations. You have now entered the first gate of the philosophers' fortress in which they dwell; proceed wisely so that you may occupy more doors of this fortress, which is round in the manner of a bell, and has eleven more gates; one has been overcome, now hasten to the second.

These, and no more, are our <term>Magnesia: an alchemical term for the primal matter or the "body" of the philosopher's stone</term>, our <term>Adrop: a term often used for lead or the "soul" of the metallic body</term>, and no others. Between these two contrary qualities, a most wonderful middle substance is generated, which is our Mercury and the unctuous <term>menstruum: a solvent or liquid agent used to dissolve solid matter</term>, our secret sulfur. It works invisibly, burning bodies more violently than fire until they are dissolved into mineral water—that which we call "night" because of its darkness, and "the North" <note>the North was associated with cold and darkness, symbolizing the initial black stage of the work</note>.

But I think you do not yet perfectly understand the true secret of the philosophers' dissolution; therefore, I advise you to grasp my words wisely, for I am about to tell you without deception what our solution is. It is the cause of our congelation <note>original: "congelationis"; the process of thickening or solidifying a liquid into a stable form</note>. For the dissolution of one bodily part causes the congelation of another spiritual part, and we dissolve into a "water that does not wet the hand" <note>a classic alchemical riddle referring to a liquid that has the properties of a metal or a spiritual substance</note>; for when the earth is reduced entirely to ash, then the water is congealed. Understand this.

For since the elements are so linked together, when a body is altered from its first form, a new form is immediately introduced. For nothing in the nature of things is stripped of all form. And here I desire to reveal a secret to you—the foundation of our entire mystery—if you are ignorant of this, you will do nothing but waste your labor and your expenses, both great and small.

Take care, therefore, that you do not fall into error: for the greater the quantity of earth and the smaller the quantity of water, the better and more quickly you will see the solution. Observe how ice is resolved into water, and rightly so, for it was water before; in the same way, our earth is reduced back into water, and the water is congealed by this forever.

For according to the opinion of all the philosophers, every metal was once mineral water; for which reason, all things are reduced into water by means of water. In this water, there are naturally four qualities fighting against each other in their diversity. Substance must be converted into substance, and quality into quality, until the diversity is reduced to a perfect unity.

For Scripture testifies that when the earth is disturbed, the mountains shall be cast into the depths of the sea. So also our bodies are finally converted into water. Thus, in this chapter, which is very brief, I have taught you the true solution. Now to the third gate, for this one is now occupied.

...so that they all may be transmuted. But I have need to write more concerning this separation. <term>Separation</term> <note>the process of isolating the different components of the "prime matter"</note> is defined by the philosophers as the fourfold dispersal of the aforementioned elements. Regarding this separation, I find a similar figure which exists among the prophets in the book of Psalms:

> God led forth a river of pure water from the rock, and oil abundantly from the hardest stone.

So also from our precious stone, if you are wise, you shall draw forth an incombustible oil and water. And concerning this business, there is no need for the blowing of coals. Do this with a gentle and nourished heat; first with a moist fire, and afterwards a dry one, extracting the <term>phlegm</term> <note>the watery, inactive byproduct of distillation</note> with patience, and afterwards the other natures wisely. Thus must you often perform the separation, dividing the matter into two parts, so that you separate the subtle from the gross, until the earth remains at the bottom with a leaden color. That earth is **fixed** <note>stable and resistant to heat</note>, so that it can endure all violence; the other part is **spiritual** and **volatile**, but all those things must be converted into one single thing. 

Then you shall distill the oil and the water from the water, and by the help of its addition—namely, of the water—you will receive movement. Observe this well, lest you ruin your work through the neglect of proper sealing. There are four kinds of fires which you ought to know: 
1. **Natural**, 
2. **Unnatural**, 
3. **Against nature**, 
4. and **Elemental**, which ignites wood. 

We use these fires, and no others. The **fire against nature** must torture the bodies; it is the **dragon**, as I tell you, burning violently like the fire of hell. The **fire of nature** is the third <term>menstruum</term> <note>a solvent capable of dissolving solids</note>; that fire is naturally present in every thing. We call the circumstantial fire "**unnatural**," such as the heat of ashes and of baths used for putrefying. Without these fires you will lead nothing to putrefaction, so that your matter may be separated, and simultaneously proportioned for the ninth conjunction. 

Therefore, make the fire inside your glass, which burns the bodies more effectively than elemental fire; if only you wish to make a profit from our secrets according to your heart's desire, then your [matter] and woman will both **putrefy and germinate**, with the help of the fire born naturally from the circumstance, so that it may afterwards be separated. In this way you must overcome the **gate of separation**; afterward you will be able to proceed further [to the way] of the secret conjunction...

### On Conjunction, the Fourth Gate

After that chapter on natural separation, through which the elements of our **Stone** <note>The Philosopher's Stone, the legendary substance capable of transmuting base metals into gold</note> are separated, there follows now the chapter of secret **conjunction**. This process joins opposing natures into a perfect unity, and so converts them that neither flees from the other; when they are examined together by fire, their marriage stands remarkably firm. The philosophers therefore define this, saying that **conjunction** is nothing other than the coupling of separated qualities, or as others prefer, a certain balancing of the principles. 

But some mix their "bodies" <note>The solid metallic materials</note> with **commercial Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurio venali"; common quicksilver bought from a shop or apothecary, which alchemists believed was "dead" compared to their prepared "Philosophical Mercury"</note> from the apothecaries, because it cannot divide their elements, and for that reason they wander from the path. For until the **soul** has been separated and purged from its **original sin** <note>The impurities or "dross" inherent in raw matter</note> with water, and purely spiritualized, you cannot achieve true conjunction. Divide therefore the soul from the body, then from the corporeal and spiritual part, the soul will cause a perpetual union. 

The philosophers make mention of two conjunctions: one is **gross**, which makes the body raw again with Mercury; but leaving this one behind, pursue the second. This second one, as I said, must be celebrated after the separation of the elements, in which the remaining parts are so bound together and reduced to a perfect temperament <note>A state of perfect balance where no single quality dominates</note> that there will never again be any conflict between them. Thus separation is the cause of true conjunction of **water** and **air** with **earth** and **fire**, so that each element can be transformed into the other; and so they will persist forever according to your heart's desire. Do as the potters do with clay and mud: temper them until they are thick, and not too diluted, so you will reach dryness more quickly. 

But there are three kinds of this conjunction. The first is called **double** by the philosophers, which exists between the active and the passive, the male and the female; **Mercury** and **living sulfur**; matter and form; the thin and the thick joined together. This instruction will certainly help you to correctly complete our conjunction. The second kind is called **triple**, which is a conjunction made of three things: **body**, **soul**, and **spirit**, until they agree among themselves; you must transform this triad into a **monad** <note>A single, indivisible unit or "One"</note>. For just as the soul must be the bond of the spirit, so also the bo-

The fourth type of conjunction, which is also the last, joins the four elements so that they remain as one; the philosophers rightly call it "quadruple," as does <margin>=</margin>**Guido de Montanor** <note>An influential, though somewhat obscure, 14th-century alchemist often cited for his expertise on the "Stone."</note> spiritually, whose name is spread far and wide. For whoever always adds raw material to that which is already cooked, opening his vessel and letting the matter grow cold, does not nourish the conceived seed, but deceives himself and ruins his whole work.

Therefore, if you desire success, seal the womb and nourish your seed well with constant and tempered heat, if you wish to make progress. <margin>—</margin>When the vessel has stood for five months, so that after all the clouds and eclipses the light appears, then immediately increase the heat until your **Stone** shines through with clear brightness. Only then may you immediately open your vessel and nourish the offspring that has now been born to you, with milk and food, more and more. For then **moisture** and **dryness** are so tempered that the earth has received the impression from the <margin>=</margin>water, so that they can never again be separated from each other. And just as the water gave the earth entry so that they both choose to dwell together openly, the water has acquired for itself the retentive power of the earth. Thus those two, having become one, are never again at odds. 

In this way, our whole intention depends on two things: **dryness** and **moisture**, which are two opposites. In dryness, which leads moisture to **fixation** <note>The process of making a volatile substance stable and resistant to fire.</note>; and in moisture, which induces the **liquefaction** of the earth, so that from these things thus tempered, a "balanced state" <note>original: "temperies"; a perfectly proportioned mixture of qualities.</note> may be born—not as dense as a body, nor as thin as water. Without doubt, **dissolution** and **connection** <note>Commonly known by the Latin maxim *Solve et Coagula*; the fundamental alchemical cycle of breaking down and rebuilding.</note> are the two principles of this arduous science...

### *On Putrefaction: The Fifth Gate.*

Here begins the chapter on putrefaction, without which hinge neither the crop nor the seed is multiplied; however, this must be done solely through the continuous action of heat in the body, not by manual labor <margin>—</margin> <note>original: "non manuali". The author emphasizes that putrefaction is a natural internal process triggered by heat, rather than something the alchemist does by physical stirring or manipulation.</note>. For all bodies cannot be naturally altered without it, as Christ is witness, saying: 
> Unless a grain of wheat dies, it will produce no increase in the earth, 
<note>original: "Nisi granum tritici moriatur..." A reference to John 12:24, used here to explain that matter must "die" (decompose) to be reborn in a higher form.</note> 
likewise, unless the matter putrefies, it can in no way be rightly altered, nor can the elements be naturally divided, nor can their union be absolute. Therefore, lest you perhaps labor in vain <note>original: "actū agas" — a Latin idiom meaning to do what has already been done or to waste effort.</note>, understand the principles of putrefaction correctly before you approach this work. Putrefaction can be defined in this way according to the philosophers: it is the destruction of bodies, and in our composite, the division of three things; you shall lead the destroyed bodies to corruption, and afterwards render them fit for generation. 

For whatever is generated on earth is, without a doubt, <margin>—</margin> generated by the rotation of the heavens; and so, mix your elements, equalize them wisely, and keep them in a temperate heat. Before all things, take care lest they be reduced to ashes by excessive heat—a dry, reddish, and useless powder—but instead into a black powder, like a raven's beak <note>original: "corui rostro similem". This refers to the **Nigredo** stage, where the matter turns deep black, signaling the successful death of the old form.</note>, in a warm bath <term>balneum</term>, or otherwise in our dung <term>fimus</term> <margin>—</margin> <note>Horse dung was frequently used in alchemy as a source of gentle, consistent, "moist" heat for incubation.</note>, for a period of ninety nights. Conserve these diligently in moist heat: soon after, the **blackness** will be your sign that they are hastening toward putrefaction. Afterwards, you will easily lead it through various colors to perfect **whiteness** <term>albedo</term>, and your seed will be multiplied in its own nature. 

Make them embrace and kiss one another, and let them play like children rolling up and down; and when their linens are fouled by washing, then the woman is bound to wash them. She, having often fallen ill, will fall into a faint, and finally she will die with all her infants and go into purgatory, so that she may be purged of original sin. When they are there, little by little their pains are increased, with the heat always increased more and more, which must never cease. A furnace well-suited for this business is prepared, which the wise call an **Athanor** <term>Athanor</term> <note>A specialized alchemical furnace designed to maintain a constant, steady heat over long periods without needing constant attention.</note>, keeping the heat, as is fitting, most temperate, with

Having been plunged into the depths, it does not rot quickly—believe me, or one who is experienced. For if it remains under water for a hundred years or more, you will find it just as whole as it was before. But if it is sometimes wet and sometimes dry—as you can observe through experience with wood—in the course of time that oak rots. So also stands our opinion: that sometimes our tree should be burned by the Sun, and then immediately afterward cooled with water. For in this way you will easily lead it to putrefaction <note>In alchemy, putrefaction is the "nigredo" or black stage where the substance "dies" and decays to release its essence</note>. For being now in moisture, and now again in dryness; now in great heat, and now again in cold, will cause it to rot very quickly, and then your gold will immediately putrefy. You shall treat the bodies as I have told you. And in the process of putrefaction with heat, do not be too hasty, lest you later search for your profit among the ashes. Therefore, extract the water from the earth, and with it make the soul ascend; then press it down again into the same earth, so that they descend as many times as they ascend. Defend your glass vessel from violent heat and sudden cold, and use such a moderate fire that by this means your matter never turns to glass <note>original: "vitreſcat"—this refers to vitrification, an irreversible state where the materials melt into a useless glassy slag due to excessive heat</note>. For whatever some sophist <note>original: "ſophiſta"—here meaning a deceptive or false alchemist who uses complicated recipes to hide their lack of knowledge</note> might babble, our sulfur and Mercury are in metals alone, which they indeed call oils and waters, birds and beasts, and many other names, so that the foolish may never recognize our stone. But if God grants that you should someday obtain this science through the teaching we have given you, do not reveal it to anyone, whoever they may be who asks—neither for favor, nor for silver, nor even for gold. Do not be an oppressor, a lecher, or an impudent boaster, but serve God, and let the poor be your care, if you wish to live long upon the earth. Now in this chapter I have taught you the way in which your bodies must be putrefied; therefore, direct your steps toward the sixth gate. For the fifth is now completed.

It is the hardening of soft things into a white color, and the fixing of volatile spirits. Do not be overly anxious about how you will congeal, for the elements are immediately joined together, provided that the putrefaction was performed naturally. But congelations occur in various ways—of spirits and bodies dissolved into clear water, and of salts...

likewise of things dissolved twice or three times, and then congealed into a fluid matter, about which congelations <note>Congelation in alchemy is the process of making a liquid substance solid or semi-solid without losing its ability to melt or "flow" like wax</note> fools chatter much. And some dissolve by manually dividing the elements, and afterward congealing them into a dry powder. But we do not seek such a congelation, because it is entirely contrary to our work. For our congelation does not fear the fire, since it must always remain unctuous <note>original: "vnctuoſa"—oily or fatty; in alchemy, this suggests the substance possesses "radical moisture" that prevents it from turning into dry ash</note> within it, and also abound in its tincture <note>original: "tinctura"—the transformative essence that allows the Stone to change the color and nature of other metals</note>; when congealed in the air, it must not melt into water, for then our work would be destroyed. Furthermore, it is not congealed into a stone as hard as glass or crystal, which are melted only by the violence of fire, but rather like wax, which melts quickly without the blast of bellows. Take care not to be deceived, for such a congelation is not suited to our purpose—one that returns again into water like congealed salts—but rather one that flows and remains permanent. Such congelations of salts are of no use to us; for they belong to the sophists <note>The author uses "sophists" to describe charlatans or "puffers" who perform superficial chemical tricks rather than the true Hermetic Art</note> who congeal in the common way. Therefore, if you desire to act rightly, since your medicine will never naturally flow nor be congealed unless you first putrefy, first purge, and fix the elements of our stone until they are congealed together and flow easily. For when the matter has been made white, then the spirits will be congealed with the bodies; you must still set a long term of time before such a congelation appears to you in the likeness of pearls. Rejoice at the sight of such a congelation, which afterward will bring forth grains red like blood, to be preferred above all the riches of the world. Therefore, once the thickness of the earth has been mortified <note>mortified: the alchemical death of the base material, stripping it of its coarse, physical qualities</note>, blackness is generated in the moisture. No mortal will deny this principle; indeed, all natural philosophers say so. Once this blackness is obtained, there is no reason for you to doubt the whiteness; and if you have once congealed it into whiteness, you possess the most precious stone of all stones. And just as the dry was putrefied by the moist (which causes the blackness to appear in color), so indeed, the moist congealed by the dry generates a whiteness shining most clearly at night; and dryness proceeds and whitens the matter, just as moisture shows itself in the black, with various colors always new and new again. The cause of all these things is a most temperate heat, working and moving the matter continually; and in this way, the matter is altered through this heat, both internally and externally in its substance—not as the fools do for the sake of a sophistic appearance, but here so that every part may endure any fire, being fluid, fixed, and stable in its tincture. As for the bodily part prepared by nature into a man, it is then just as its initiator was; although it was altered from one thing into another in this way, it did not, however, go outside its species, for it was consistent with the other species. You can also read another example of this in vegetable things, considering how any plant grows from its own seed by means of heat and moisture through a natural operation. Similarly, even **minerals** are nourished by their **radical moisture** <note>original: "humido radicali"; the essential, life-giving fluid that alchemists believed existed within all matter</note>, which was their beginning, not departing from their species within one and the same vessel. There we again convert one thing into another—into its mother, namely the water, when they are transferred. If this principle is ignored, you labor in vain. For then the whole is nothing other than **seed** <note>original: "sperma"</note>, nor is there anything besides it, except species with species, two in number, **male** and **female**, **agent** and **patient**, in the **womb** <note>original: "matrice"</note> of the most precious earth; and these are converted by color from one thing to another, in one glass vessel, and so from state to state, until nature leads them into one substance, from **regenerated water**. And thus the seed is altered within its species, fit to multiply its own species in likeness, just as all other things do naturally within their species. During the time of this said natural process, while the conceived seed grows, the substance is nourished by its own **menstruum** <note>original: "menstruo"; here used in the alchemical sense of a solvent or nutritive fluid that dissolves the "embryo" of the Stone</note>, which only water and earth produced, the color of which is **green** in its proper appearance. Lady **Venus** <note>Associated with copper, but also the force of attraction and transformation</note> will be able to open the truth of this to you, if you call upon her as an advisor from the beginning. This secret is hidden from the highest and lowest philosophers. This blood, extracted from the aforementioned lion, did not have a perfect **digestion** <note>original: "concoctionem"</note> due to a lack of heat. This blood is called our **secret menstruum**, with which our seed is nourished temperately, when it is converted into bodily dregs, and becomes white, and perfe— <note>The text cuts off mid-word ("perfectum")</note>

<header>THE SECOND WHEEL</header>

When it is perfectly dry, congealed, and fixed in its own body, then the **twice-cooked blood** <note>original: "bis coctus sanguis"; a metaphor for the refined, reddened matter of the stone</note> can be clearly seen, which is called the **whitest Diadem** <note>original: "albissimum Diadema"</note> of this work. Understand now that our **fiery water** <note>original: "ignea nostra aqua"</note>, thus sharpened, is called **menstrual water** <note>original: "menstrualis aqua"; in alchemy, this refers to a potent solvent or "first matter," not literal blood</note>, in which our earth is dissolved and naturally **calcined** <note>reduced to a fine powder through heat</note> through congelation, so that they can never be divided. Yet, you shall not cease to congeal more waters—three parts of sharpened water, as said before, with a fourth part of congealed earth, and no more. From here, add to the substance thus congealed a fourth part of **Crystalline water**, and make them join in a mutual marriage through congelation into a metallic medium. This will shine like a well-polished sword, appearing after the **blackness** <note>original: "nigredinem"; the *nigredo* stage of decomposition</note> that will show first. Then give it a fourth part of new water. You must still perform many more **imbibitions** <note>original: "imbibitiones"; the process of repeatedly soaking a dry substance with liquid until it is absorbed</note>. Give it a second, and then even a third, keeping the stated proportion in your mind; then hasten to the fourth time, and do not omit the fifth and sixth. Put in two parts for each of those three times, and on the seventh time it must have five parts. When you have completed seven imbibitions, you must again turn the wheel and **putrefy** <note>allow to rot or break down</note> all that matter without adding anything. First watch for the blackness, then congeal the whole into **whiteness** <note>original: "albedinem"; the *albedo* stage</note>; then you have brought the base to its end. Afterward, ascend into the **redness** <note>original: "rubedinem"; the *rubedo* or final stage</note> through the "midday." Thus your water is divided into two parts: with the first part, the bodies are putrefied. The second part is destined for the imbibitions, with which the matter is afterward blackened and immediately whitened over a gentle fire; then it is called by the philosophers the **Sun of celestial splendor** <note>original: "Sol caelestis fulgoris"</note>. Lead it back to redness, and so you have conquered the **sixth gate**.

## *On feeding, the seventh gate.* <note>original: "De cibatione, porta septima"</note>

Now I turn my pen to the description of **feeding** <note>original: "cibationis"; the stage of nourishing the stone to increase its power</note>. Behold, it must occupy the seventh place, but it must be explained in few words; therefore pay attention and listen to me diligently. Feeding is what we call the nourishing of our dry matter with **milk and food** <note>alchemical metaphors for the liquid and solid components</note>, both given in moderation until it is reduced into the third order. But never give it so much that you suffocate it; beware of **dropsy** <note>original: "hydropisi"; a medical condition of swelling, used here to mean "too much liquid"</note> and of **Noah’s flood**. Therefore, add food and drink to it little by little, as it seems beneficial to it, lest the watery humors overcome the blood. For this reason, the drink is so measured that it never [extinguishes...] <note>original catchword: "exstin-"</note> the natural appetite.

->*On sublimation, the eighth gate.*<-

Here I shall speak a word or two about our **sublimation** <note>the process of heating a substance until it vaporizes and then becomes solid again</note>, which is the eighth gate. Fools indeed sublimate. But do not you sublimate in that way: For we certainly do not sublimate like they do. To sublimate rightly, therefore, you will not err if you first know how to make the body spiritual, and then make your spirits corporal <note>this refers to the alchemical goal of making solids volatile and fixing volatile gases into solids</note>, as I have taught. Some sublimate **Mercury** from vitriol and salt, and other spirits from scales of iron and steel, from eggshells, and from quicklime <note>original: "calce viua"</note>, and in their own way they sublimate correctly; but such sublimation is not at all suited to our intention: for we do not sublimate in that way, and so we now proceed toward true sublimation. In sublimation, first beware of this one thing: do not sublimate to the very top of the vessel, for without violence you will not force it back to the bottom, but it wishes to adhere and remain there: thus it delights in the cooling. Therefore, keep it with a temperate heat from below for the space of forty days until it is black and dark: for then the soul begins to go forth from its own veins: for whatever is subtle will undoubtedly ascend with the spirit. Now we perform sublimation for three reasons: the first is so that the body may become spiritual; the second so that the spirit may become corporeal, and be fixed with it, and become of the same substance; the third reason is so that it may be purged from its original impurity, and its sulfurous saltiness in which it is infected may be diminished. Then, when these have been purged together, they shall be sublimed on high, **whiter than snow**; that sight will be most pleasing to you: for then you will immediately and perfectly know that the spirit will be **precipitated** <note>rendered solid or brought down from its gaseous state</note>: then the **eighth gate** will lie open to you, from which many have been excluded with mockery.

->*On fermentation, the ninth gate.*<-

Few operators understand true **fermentation**, wherefore I shall explain this secret to you. I have indeed traveled through many regions before I could find one who could explain it to me; at last, by divine favor, whose name be blessed, I arrived at perfect knowledge. Pay attention, therefore, to what I am about to write here: fermentations are done in various ways, by which our **medicine** <note>the alchemical Elixir or Stone</note> is perpetuated. Some dissolve the **Sun** and **Moon** <note>original: "Solem & Lunam"; the alchemical symbols for Gold and Silver</note> into clear water, and with their medicine they cause them to be congealed; however, when these are examined in the fire, they cannot endure, nor be altered to completion. Such fermentation is not our purpose. Some act more naturally, fermenting their medicine in this way: dissolving the Sun and Moon in **Mercury** <note>Quicksilver</note> until they rise up with the spirits, subliming them together twice or thrice. Then with these they perform fermentation. That is a certain way, which we nevertheless reject. Some are more fortunate in choosing the truth regarding fermentation; they **amalgamate** <note>mix a metal with mercury to form a soft paste</note> the bodies with Mercury in the manner of a paste, then they cast their medicines upon them. These people have some knowledge of our secrets...

...[perfec]tion, but not a true one with a complete fulfillment, because they neither putrefy nor alter their own **ferment** <note>In alchemy, a "ferment" is a substance (often gold or silver) added to the "Stone" to give it a specific direction or "flavor," much like yeast is added to dough.</note>: therefore I reveal to you this secret: see how you acted upon the **imperfect bodies** <note>Base metals like lead or tin</note>; do exactly the same in all things with the **perfect bodies** <note>Gold and silver</note>. Then perform the **projection** <note>The final stage where the medicine is cast upon base metal to transmute it</note> as it pleases you, because the medicine is then altogether perfect. In this way, you shall make both the red and the white ferment.

For just as wheat flour reduced into a mass requires ferment <note>yeast/leaven</note> so that the bread can have its natural taste and be a most suitable nourishment for man, so also you shall ferment your work, so that you may taste of the pure ferment, capable of enduring all trials forever.

And know that there are three ferments: two of the bodies in a pure nature which must be altered as we have told you; the third and most secret one, which we meditate upon, is that **first earth** with its own proper **green water** <note>original: "aqua viridi"; likely a reference to the "Green Lion" or Vitriol, a potent acidic solvent used in the early stages of the Work</note>. Regarding this, if I wished to raise a question and ask practitioners what this thing is, I would soon test them by this: whether they have true knowledge of our fermentation.

True fermentation, therefore, as I tell you, is the incorporation of the soul with the body, restoring to it its natural odor, taste, and color through the natural thickening of separated things by a rightful reintegration. By this, the body receives an impression from the spirit, so that each can help the other to achieve a harmonious entry. For just as the body, in its physical frame, cannot effectively show its qualities until it has been made spiritual, so neither can the spirits remain with the body before they themselves are proportionally fixed with it. For then the body teaches the spirit to endure the fire, and the spirit teaches the body to enter and penetrate at your pleasure. For that reason, you must ferment your **Sun** [Gold] with the **Sun**, using its own water—by which I mean the purified earth—which is nothing else to say than ele... <note>The text cuts off mid-word; likely "elementa" (elements).</note>

For just as the **Magnet** <note>original: "Magnes"; the author uses the magnet as a metaphor for the natural attraction between the "earthly" body of the stone and its "spiritual" component</note>, as you see, draws iron to itself, so our earth by nature draws downward its soul, which had been raised from itself with the wind. Earth is gold, and so is the soul—not the common gold of the marketplace, but our **elementated** <note>A substance reduced to its purest elemental state</note> kind; yet the **Sun** <note>original: "Sol"; Gold</note> must be joined to these, so that it may be altered by our wheel. Namely, so that you may putrefy and alter those things I told you, before you begin to ferment your medicine, see that you renew the Sun and **Moon** <note>original: "Lunam"; Silver</note>, so that they themselves may hold some of the **quintessence** <note>original: "quinta essentia"; the "fifth element," a celestial and incorruptible essence beyond the four physical elements</note>; then their **tincture** <note>The color-giving and transformative power of the medicine</note> will endure perpetually.

There is also another most excellent way pertaining to another operation: we make a most fragrant water, with which we reduce all bodies into a flowing oil, with which we make our medicine. We call this water the quintessence, which heals all the infirmities of men. But this must be done with your **base** <note>original: "basi"</note> prepared according to our teaching, which is our **lime** <note>original: "calx"; the powdered remains after a substance has been heated/calcined</note>; for when bodies are thus calcined, that water immediately dissolves them into oil. Therefore, make oil from the Sun and Moon, which is a ferment most fragrant in scent. The ninth gate of this citadel has been overcome.

### *On exaltation, the tenth gate.*

Let us now follow the chapter on **exaltation** <note>original: "exaltationis"; the process of raising a substance to a higher "dignity" or potency, often through repeated refinement</note>, of which you must have perfect knowledge, for it differs little from sublimation, if you have understood our words. To this the Holy Scripture is suited, where Christ says: *“I, if I be lifted up, will draw all things to myself.”* <note>A reference to John 12:32, used here as a chemical allegory for the "Stone" drawing the qualities of other metals into itself</note>

If we have exalted our medicine in this manner, it will be ennobled by this reasoning. This ought to be done in two ways, from that time in which the parts are **betrothed** <note>joined together</note>, which are **crucified** <note>Subjected to the "death" of chemical breakdown</note>, and examined, and the male and female are **buried** <note>original: "contumulantur"; placed together in the sealed vessel</note> together, and afterwards revived by the **spirit of life** <note>original: "spiritu vitæ"</note>. Then it must be exalted upward into heaven, so that there the body and soul may be glorified. For you must bring it to such subtlety that they ascend together to be enthroned in the shining clouds, joined with the angels.

...then they will draw all other bodies to their own proper dignity, as you will see. If, therefore, you wish to exalt your bodies, first augment them with the spirit of life until the earth is thoroughly refined through the natural rectification <note>A process of purification, usually through repeated distillation</note> of all the elements, exalting them upward into the firmament <note>In the alchemical laboratory, the "firmament" often refers to the upper part of the glass vessel where vapors collect</note>. Then they will be far more precious than gold because of the quintessence <note>original: "quinta essentia"; the fifth element or pure spirit that exists beyond the four physical elements</note> they contain. For when cold overcomes heat, air is converted into water; thus two opposites are brought together until they are properly balanced with one another. Likewise, as I have told you, water is converted into air when heat dominates cold through the art of our circulation. Then you will obtain air from fire by dissolving, putrefying, and subliming; and you obtain fire from material earth by separating the elements in turn, specifically by thoroughly calcining <term>calcining: the process of heating a substance to high temperatures in a crucible to remove impurities and reduce it to a powder</term> the earth. When each part has been purified, then they all partake of the quintessence.

In this way, cause the elements to circulate, swiftly exalting one into the other. Perform all of this in a single, well-sealed glass vessel—not by manual labor, but naturally, as I am teaching you. First, diligently convert fire into water. For fire exists in the air, which in turn exists in the water; this conversion is well-suited to our purpose. 

Then turn your wheel <note>The "wheel" refers to the repetitive cycle of vaporization and condensation within the flask</note> further until the air is converted into earth. This is most easily achieved, for air exists in water, which exists in the earth. Though they are opposites in quality, you can quickly convert water into fire as well, for water exists in the earth, and the earth exists in the fire. This is true conversion.

The wheel is now nearly fully turned. Convert the water into earth, which is the proper "nest" or foundation for the other elements; for the earth is within the fire, which in turn rests within the air. You must begin this circulation in the West, then move toward the South until the elements are exalted. Proceed carefully, as I have shown you in the diagram <note>Referring to the circular diagrams common in alchemical texts illustrating the relationships between elements</note>. In this progression, you can clearly see that there is no passage from one extreme to another except through an intervening medium, since they possess opposite qualities. 

Indeed, reason dictates that heat cannot be converted into cold—nor any other opposites into one another—without a mediating element, such as moisture, which links the hot and the cold, as I have told you before. Thus far, I have taught you how to perform the perfect circulation of all your elements. You have an example in the figure of the wheel showing how to achieve this exaltation and the true gradation <term>gradation: the process of intensifying the properties, such as color or "nobility," of the substance</term> of your medicine into the elements, until you have brought it to a balanced temperament. At that point, you have mastered the **Tenth Gate**.
